papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic Analysis Suggests Inflammatory Heterogeneity and Stromal-Epithelial Transcriptional Differences in Peri-Implantitis Tissues.
papers.abstract: AimTo explore spatial inflammatory heterogeneity and associated stromal-epithelial transcriptional differences in peri-implantitis tissues using high-resolution spatial transcriptomics.Materials and methodsThis exploratory study applied Visium HD spatial transcriptomics to five peri-implantitis lesions and four tooth-associated healthy gingival reference tissues. Spatial barcodes were annotated by histology, marker expression and module scoring. BANKSY, GASTON, differential expression, Gene Ontology, public scRNA-seq reanalysis, CellChat and multiplex immunofluorescence were used to assess inflammatory niches, stromal and epithelial gradients, epithelial gene sets and inferred signalling.ResultsPeri-implantitis lesions showed descriptively greater immune-cell enrichment in an unmatched comparison with tooth-associated gingival reference tissue. Fibroblasts in inflammation-enriched niches differed from stromal-region fibroblasts and COL11A1-positive fibroblasts localised near immune-rich areas. GASTON identified graded expression patterns along the epithelial-stromal interface and epithelial regions. An 11-gene epithelial-inflammation-associated set showed region-associated expression differences, with supportive expression trends in public epithelial scRNA-seq data. CellChat suggested descriptively increased epithelial outgoing signalling involving WNT5A, MIF and ANXA1.ConclusionsThis study spatially describes host responses in peri-implantitis, including regional inflammatory heterogeneity, fibroblast-state variation and epithelial transcriptional differences. The epithelial-inflammation-associated gene set requires further validation. Interpretation should account for the small sample size, tooth-associated gingival reference tissue, absence of microbiome profiling and barcode-level Visium HD data.

papers.title: Mesoscale molecular architecture of the striatum across cell types and adult aging.
papers.abstract: The human striatum governs diverse motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors yet lacks the obvious cytoarchitectural boundaries defining functional territories elsewhere in the brain. Using Slide-tags single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics, we profiled 1.1 million cells across 19 postmortem donors to uncover the striatum's spatial organization. These data revealed a consistent subdivision of the striatum into six zones, each defined by molecularly distinct populations of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) and featuring spatially coordinated neuron-astrocyte interaction networks. To determine their structural relevance, we generated a companion mouse spatial atlas that identified four homologous zones that aligned with territories defined by brain-wide afferent projections. Finally, imputing zonal identities onto a 131-donor single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cohort revealed that dorsal zones exhibit the greatest age-related transcriptional change and that the expression differences defining zonation attenuate with age. This resource establishes a conserved mesoscale spatial framework for the mammalian striatum, linking single-cell molecular identity to structural connectomics and aging.

papers.title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide whether a niche atlas is translational or merely descriptive. Methods. We assembled MuSpec , an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder, and applied it to two single-cell-resolution Stereo-seq slides from human TB lung: B1 (pulmonary granuloma; Y40012NC13; 36,382 cells) and P1 (peri-lesional lung; Y40012LA11; 51,834 cells). Each cell was represented as a 39-dimensional input (7-dimensional cell-type composition from cell2location deconvolution against a 146,345-cell peripheral-blood scRNA-seq reference, 30 expression principal components, and 2 spatial coordinates). MuSpec smooths the input at three kNN scales (k = 10/20/30), rasterises each scale onto a ≤ 224² lattice, and passes the three feature maps through four deep-learning modules built on published attention-and-fusion designs — ASFF cross-scale fusion, TripletAttention, ExternalAttention, and a Fourier graph network (FGN) — to produce a 16-dimensional niche embedding; a shared encoder is trained jointly across both slides with an MSE reconstruction loss plus a spatial-smoothing loss, and niches are obtained by KMeans (K = 9). We benchmarked MuSpec against BANKSY at matched numbers of spatial domains, ran a three-seed module ablation and a 34-configuration single-factor hyperparameter sweep, and used the recovered granuloma signature for multi-library signature-reversal drug repurposing (LINCS L1000 chemical perturbations, GEO perturbations, NIBR DRUGseq 2025, and the original CMAP, merged) and AutoDock Vina docking against the host target SP110. Results. MuSpec produced a compact, sub-million-parameter model (782,251 parameters; 93.9% in ASFF) that trains in minutes on a single consumer GPU (≈ 7 GB peak). On every matched-K comparison, MuSpec embeddings separated niches far more sharply than BANKSY (Δsilhouette + 0.31 to + 0.40 on both slides); MuSpec’s own K = 9 silhouette was 0.322 (B1) and 0.285 (P1). Three-seed ablation showed that no module was removable losslessly : removing ExternalAttention lowered niche separation (Δsilhouette − 0.093) but raised robustness and cross-slide transfer (Δ of + 0.137 to + 0.362), identifying a clean separation↔robustness trade-off. For normalisation, a three-seed paired design showed that 7 of 8 robustness metrics changed sign across seeds, so we report no seed-stable difference between global and per-slide normalisation, with only a small stable (+ 0.010 ± 0.003) silhouette advantage to per-slide normalisation on B1. The hyperparameter sweep revealed a monotone separation–robustness frontier with no cliffs, on which the default setting was the robustness optimum (mean noise-robustness ARI 0.758; drop-composition ARI 0.683 on B1 and 0.518 on P1, the highest in the sweep). Joint niche characterisation recovered myeloid/granuloma (SPP1, MMP9, CTSK), airway/club (MUC5B, SCGB1A1, BPIFB1), fibrotic (SFRP2, COL1A1, INHBA) and fibroblast (IL11, TFPI2, PI16) niches, and an SP110–IFN hub analysis. A 324-gene granuloma signature (233 up, 91 down) yielded top signature-reversal hits led by a PPARγ-agonist trio (pioglitazone 90.08, troglitazone, rosiglitazone), and in-silico docking of a focused 6-ligand panel against SP110 gave the strongest affinities for withaferin A (− 7.18 kcal/mol) and nintedanib (− 6.92 kcal/mol). Conclusions. MuSpec provides an unsupervised, reproducible, computationally light route to spatially resolved niche atlases in infectious-disease tissue, and its systematic benchmarking exposes a separation↔robustness trade-off that should be reported rather than hidden. Applied to human TB lung, it recovered biologically coherent, cross-slide-conserved granuloma niches and nominated host-directed repurposing candidates.

papers.title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
papers.abstract: BackgroundProgression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation.ResultsHSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903, respectively. Higher risk scores were associated with hypoxia, glycolysis, TGF-β/EMT signaling, stromal remodeling, and reduced adaptive immune programs. MK-2206 showed favorable predicted interactions with MIF and CXCL8, with greater modeled stability for the CXCL8 complex. Immunohistochemistry confirmed progressively increased CXCL8 and MIF expression from normal cervix to HSIL and SCC.ConclusionProgression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

papers.title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes.
papers.abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. Regulated cell death (RCD) and dead-cell clearance form a critical mechanistic layer within this network. Efficient efferocytosis of apoptotic cells reinforces resolution and tolerance, whereas necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis disrupt cell membranes and release danger signals that reshape myeloid activation, T-cell function, and the tumor microenvironment. In liver transplantation, this tolerogenic tendency produces donor-specific hyporesponsiveness, allowing a selected subset of stable recipients to stop immunosuppression while maintaining graft function-a state called operational tolerance. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), tumors exploit the same immunosuppressive axes to block anti-tumor T-cell infiltration and effector function. Anti-PD-L1 therapy combined with anti-angiogenic treatment improves survival, demonstrating that partial disruption of tumor immunosuppression is therapeutically effective. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell sequencing reveal that SPP1-positive macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts form a tumor immune barrier that excludes lymphocytes, showing that hepatic tolerance is organized in space. This duality becomes most dangerous in HCC recurrence after liver transplantation, where immune checkpoint inhibitors boost anti-tumor immunity but also raise the risk of acute rejection, graft failure, and death. Unlike reviews focused on hepatic immune tolerance, regulated cell death, or HCC immunobiology in isolation, this review integrates these processes across the physiological liver, transplantation, HCC, and post-transplant recurrence. We define this coordinated hyporesponsive state as the liver immune tolerance program (ITP), generated by cellular, molecular, spatial, metabolic, and cell-death-related networks. Rather than treating these processes separately, we position RCD and dead-cell clearance as a "death-to-immunity axis," systematically compare ITP remodeling in the physiological liver, transplantation, and HCC, and use post-transplant HCC recurrence as a clinical crossover setting in which graft protection and antitumor immune surveillance become therapeutic considerations. On this basis, we propose precision immune homeostasis: rather than choosing between immunosuppression and immune activation, immune status should be adjusted to an individualized range that protects the graft while preserving anti-tumor immune surveillance.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia.
papers.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Additionally, we identify core-shell organization of the internal globus pallidus. This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.

papers.title: Principles and assumptions underlying domain detection in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial-omics technologies simultaneously measure feature expression and locations within tissues, providing an unprecedented opportunity to study tissue structures. The first key step in analyzing these high-dimensional datasets is identifying biologically relevant clusters, yet the large number of spatial-omics clustering (SOC) methods makes method selection challenging. Here we comprehensively review 47 SOC methods and extract information on 108 variables across 26 groups of method characteristics and applicability. This revealed substantial diversity in the underlying algorithms, affecting the suitability of methods to different tissues and biotechnologies. Based on this, we provide an analytical decision tree to help data analysts select methods based on their data types and research questions, and we highlight knowledge gaps to help bioinformaticians identify new avenues for method development. We thus hope to pave the way for more effective applications in a diverse methodological landscape and guide future method development.

papers.title: Identification of immune- and cellular senescence-related genes in keloids through integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveKeloids are pathological scars resulting from abnormal connective tissue growth in the skin. Although cellular senescence has been implicated in fibrotic diseases, its role and molecular characteristics in keloids remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify cellular senescence-related genes associated with keloid pathogenesis and investigate their potential relationships with alterations in the immune microenvironment.MethodsPublicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE44270 and GSE92566) and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (GSE181297) from the Gene Expression Omnibus database were integrated for analysis. Cellular senescence-related genes were obtained from the CellAge database and intersected with differentially expressed genes identified between keloid and normal samples to obtain cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes. Protein-protein interaction network analysis was performed to identify hub genes, which were further intersected with single-cell differentially expressed genes to determine key genes. Immune infiltration was assessed using the Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts algorithm, and cellular senescence-associated biological pathways were evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and gene set variation analysis. The expression patterns and cellular distribution of key genes were further evaluated using single-cell sequencing data.ResultsA total of 18 cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes were identified between keloid and normal samples. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified 10 hub genes, and integration with single-cell transcriptomic data revealed 5 key genes associated with cellular senescence: cyclin D1, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8, galectin 3, and notch receptor 3. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression between keloid and normal groups across the combined bulk-transcriptomic datasets. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated significant associations between key genes and immune cell characteristics. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A was correlated with gamma delta T cells and resting dendritic cells, whereas notch receptor 3 was associated with CD8+ T cells and naive CD4+ T cells. Single-cell analysis further characterized the expression patterns of key genes across different cell populations in keloid tissues.ConclusionThis study provides an integrated transcriptomic and single-cell landscape of cellular senescence-related alterations in keloids. The identified key genes are associated with cellular senescence-related transcriptional changes and immune microenvironment characteristics in keloid tissues. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression patterns at the bulk-transcriptome level, suggesting their relevance in keloid pathogenesis. These findings highlight the potential involvement of cellular senescence-associated programs in the interplay between fibroblast activation and immune alterations in keloids and provide candidate genes for further functional investigation.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined neuropathologically by the presence of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, yet these canonical lesions alone cannot account for its clinical, regional and cellular heterogeneity. AD is a multicellular, spatially organized disease shaped by the interactions of neurons, glia and vascular cells within distinct anatomical microenvironments. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have made it possible to dissect the transcriptional signatures of individual cell populations in the AD brain, revealing selective neuronal vulnerability, stage-dependent glial remodelling and widespread disruption of cell-cell communication networks, whereas spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging have anchored these molecular changes to their tissue context. Studies of defined populations, such as people with autosomal-dominant AD or Down syndrome-associated AD, and of the oldest-old cohorts help disentangle the molecular changes that are causal drivers from those that are downstream consequences. Across individuals, AD heterogeneity is further shaped by sex and ancestry, underscoring the need for broader representation of these factors in single-cell and spatial studies. These advances are also reshaping translational pipelines through multi-omic benchmarking of animal models and single-cell-based drug-repurposing strategies. Thus, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are redefining our understanding of AD heterogeneity and informing precision approaches to treatment.

papers.title: Spatially integrated transcriptomics maps the metastatic niche in lymph nodes of gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) metastasis is a major determinant of clinical outcome in gastric cancer (GC), yet the molecular and spatial features of metastatic LN niches remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated digital spatial profiling (DSP) of primary GC and matched LNs, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Deconvolution showed enrichment of exhausted T cells, regulatory T cells, and fibroblasts in mLNs, consistent with immunosuppressive remodeling of the local microenvironment. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated the galectin-9 (LGALS9)-CD45/CD44, CLEC2D-KLRB1, and CCL19/CCL21-CCR7 axes in mLNs. Spatial analysis further revealed compartment-specific heterogeneity, including distinct proliferative, immune, and immunosuppressive programs. Integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets, we derived a 12-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LNMGS); high LNMGS scores were associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort. Spatial mapping of the LNMGS in primary GC identified an LNMGS-high region displaying a center-to-periphery expression gradient and tending to have a higher inferred copy-number burden. A distance-associated gene signature derived from this gradient was enriched for proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis, immune evasion, and stemness. Together, these findings provide a spatial and molecular framework for lymph node metastasis in GC and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for further investigation. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

papers.title: Single-cell insights into plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses: cellular heterogeneity and regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Plants are continuously challenged by biotic and abiotic stresses that compromise growth, productivity, and stress resilience. Although bulk omics approaches have identified numerous stress-responsive pathways, they obscure the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization that underlie stress perception, signal transmission, and response execution. Single-cell and spatial omics now enable plant stress responses to be resolved at the levels of cell type, cell state, and spatial location. In this review, we synthesize recent applications of single-cell RNA sequencing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and emerging single-cell proteomics in plant stress biology. We systematically compare biotic and abiotic stresses in terms of spatial response patterns, cellular division of labor, cell-state transitions, and gene regulatory networks. Biotic stress typically generates localized, infection-centered immune landscapes characterized by sentinel-cell activation, vascular defense hubs, and receptor-triggered transcriptional cascades. In contrast, abiotic stress more commonly involves organ-scale homeostatic adjustment, developmental plasticity, and sustained growth-tolerance trade-offs. Despite these distinctions, both stress classes share core regulatory modules, including reactive oxygen species, hormone signaling, transcription factor networks, and vascular long-distance communication. We further discuss technical challenges related to protoplast and nuclei preparation, cell-type annotation, spatial resolution, and multimodal data integration. By linking stress-responsive genes to the specific cell types, states, and spatial domains in which they function, single-cell approaches provide a mechanistic framework for precision engineering and breeding of stress-resilient crops.

papers.title: Acid-triggered carboxymethyl chitosan-stabilized synchronously mineralized collagen modified implants: Osteoimmunity regulation of bone defect repair in osteoporosis.

papers.title: Immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor axes in post-infarction cardiac remodeling: convergent and divergent mechanisms compared with cancer-associated fibroblasts.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction-triggered cardiac fibrosis is a cardinal feature of maladaptive ventricular remodeling and a principal contributor to heart failure pathogenesis. Enabled by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, accumulating evidence demonstrates that post-infarction fibrosis represents an actively coordinated biological program rather than a passive wound-healing event, which is governed by ligand-receptor-mediated crosstalk between immune cells and cardiac fibroblasts. Pioneering work has established monocyte-derived macrophages as a predominant cellular source of pro-inflammatory interleukin-1β; upon binding its cognate receptor on fibroblasts, this cytokine instigates the generation of pro-fibrotic fibroblast subsets within spatially segregated niches of the infarcted myocardium. Multiple additional ligand-receptor modules, encompassing osteopontin-CD44/integrin, transforming growth factor-β, platelet-derived growth factor, as well as growth arrest-specific protein 6-MER tyrosine kinase, further fine-tune fibroblast activation trajectories in a spatiotemporally-restricted fashion. Intriguingly, a substantial fraction of these ligand-receptor interactions are conserved in cancer-associated fibroblast biology, wherein osteopontin-producing macrophages and activated fibroblasts collaboratively build pro-tumor stromal microenvironments. We consolidate recent multi-omic findings regarding immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor communication during post-infarction cardiac remodeling, highlight mechanistic analogies to cancer-associated fibroblast activation, and discuss therapeutic prospects arising from targeting these conserved signaling nodes across cardiac and neoplastic diseases.

papers.title: Spatial and single-cell insights into the prostate cancer microenvironment: overcoming immunotherapy resistance through multidimensional strategies.
papers.abstract: Despite breakthroughs in immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) across various malignancies, prostate cancer (PCa), particularly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), has shown limited responses to ICIs. This pervasive primary resistance is fundamentally driven by the canonically "immune-cold" and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) of PCa. Propelled by recent advancements in single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, this review comprehensively deconstructs the dynamic spatiotemporal evolution of the PCa immune landscape across localized, mCRPC, and lineage-plastic variant stages (e.g., neuroendocrine and double-negative PCa). We systematically delineate how the profound immune-excluded phenotype is sculpted not by isolated events, but by an intricate, multicellular suppressive ecosystem. Specifically, we detail the subclonal heterogeneity, spatial topography, and metabolic crosstalk of key suppressive populations, including specific tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) subsets, regulatory T cells (Tregs), cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). Furthermore, we elucidate the tumor-intrinsic genetic aberrations (e.g., PTEN inactivation, TP53 mutations) and epigenetic rewiring (e.g., EZH2, CHD1, ARID1A dysregulation) that initiate and perpetually orchestrate this suppressive network. Finally, we highlight emerging therapeutic vulnerabilities and future translational directions. Dismantling the microenvironmental barriers in PCa necessitates transcending singular ICI blockade by employing novel combinatorial strategies that target chemotactic recruitment axes (e.g., CXCR2/CXCR4), reverse metabolic plasticity, and abrogate epigenetic silencing. Coupled with high-resolution liquid biopsy biomarkers (e.g., ctDNA, B7-H3+ EVs) for precise patient stratification and cutting-edge synthetic biology interventions, these multidimensional approaches hold profound promise for reversing the dual metabolic and immune suppressive state of PCa, thereby overcoming clinical immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT), yet how somatic repeat instability and HTT inclusions relate to selective cell loss in the human brain remains unclear. We have developed a multimodal spatial transcriptomics approach that enables the definition of transcriptional programs with subcellular resolution, somatic CAG repeat lengths, and eight other pathology markers, including HTT inclusions, in every cell of intact brain sections. Intranuclear inclusions were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions (250-350 CAGs) and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone. These data provide a comprehensive resource and establish a general framework for connecting repeat expansion and protein pathology across diverse cell types.

papers.title: SpaCoDA: fast compositional deconvolution maps recurrent cellular niches across hundreds of spatial transcriptomics sections
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Spot-based spatial transcriptomics such as 10x Visium measures a mixture of cells in each spot. Estimating the cell-type composition of each spot against a single-cell reference is the first step towards cell-level maps of tissue microenvironments, but the most accurate deconvolution methods are slow and memory-intensive at the scale of current atlases, and there still need an established way to make tissue niches comparable across hundreds of sections. Results We present SpaCoDA, which fits each spot by variance-weighted non-negative least squares against a reference signature, re-estimates a gene-level platform factor between iterations, and converts RNA shares into cell fractions using cell-size and marker-capture factors. Niches are identified within each section from fused compositional (Aitchison distances) and spatial distances, and their prototypes are integrated across sections into meta-niches. Across 123 simulated configurations under three reference-mismatch scenarios, SpaCoDA was the only one of nine methods ranked within the top two on all four evaluation metrics in every scenario, second to RCTD in mean rank. On 12 imaging-derived datasets with known composition (six Xenium datasets, each evaluated at two annotation levels, and six CosMx/Xenium datasets from three patients), it achieved the best mean rank in every summary, while running 4 to about 1,800-fold faster than the other eight methods (233-fold faster than RCTD by median runtime) with the lowest peak memory. Applied to 254 breast cancer and 181 glioblastoma sections (about 1.18 million spots), SpaCoDA identified 29 and 31 meta-niches, respectively. In breast cancer, the expression signature of a B-cell and plasma-cell meta-niche was associated with longer overall survival in TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC and was higher in tumors with a pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in I-SPY2. In glioblastoma, signatures of a perivascular antigen-presenting myeloid meta-niche and of a proliferative, hypoxic meta-niche were associated with shorter survival in TCGA-GBM and three CGGA glioma cohorts. Conclusions SpaCoDA combines competitive accuracy with orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost, making composition and niche analysis practical at cohort scale. It provides a practical framework for such analyses, enabling disease subtyping and the identification of novel therapeutic targets, and shows promise for clinical translation.

papers.title: A periodontal Piezo1-dependent brain-bone interoceptive circuit couples occlusal force to craniofacial bone homeostasis.
papers.abstract: The skeleton continuously monitors mechanical state to maintain tissue homeostasis, but whether such interoceptive control operates in the craniofacial skeleton remains unclear. Importantly, conditional deletion of Piezo1 in Gli1-lineage MSCs largely abolished occlusal force-dependent regulation of VMH activity, sympathetic tone, and mandibular bone homeostasis, establishing its required role in this pathway. Our findings define a Piezo1-PGE2-mediated skeletal interoceptive circuit that links occlusal force to central sympathetic control of craniofacial bone mass, revealing a potential neuromechanical strategy for preventing disuse-induced bone loss.

papers.title: Targeting the Immunometabolic Checkpoint IL4I1 Suppresses the Progression of Pathological Scars.

papers.title: A public-data spatial transcriptomic framework for invasive lung adenocarcinoma tumor ecosystems and prognosis.

ST is therefore best viewed as a discovery and mechanistic-prioritisation technology whose clinical promises-biomarker selection, biologic matching, and response monitoring-require independent cohorts, locked assays, patient-level reproducibility, and prospective outcome studies. papers.title: ASAOT: an accentuated structure-differentiated asymmetric optimal transport model for cell type and single-cell spatial mapping.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) characterizes spatiotemporal gene expression and facilitates analysis of cellular architecture and cell-cell crosstalk within tissue microenvironments. papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics for gene discovery identifies Slc13a5 as a modulator of bone mechanoadaptation.
papers.abstract: Bone is a dynamic tissue that continuously adapts its structure in response to mechanical loading, an essential process for maintaining skeletal health. However, this adaptive capacity declines with aging, contributing to increased fragility and fracture risk. Conditional deletion of Slc13a5 in osteolineage cells using Osteocalcin-Cre in female mice significantly increased the loading-induced mineralizing surface in tensile regions compared with Cre- Slc13a5fl/fl littermates. In addition, Slc13a5 cKO mice exhibited lower resorption around the neutral axis after loading compared to controls. Together, these findings identify Slc13a5 as a regulator of bone adaptation in regions experiencing low mechanical stimulation and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target for conditions characterized by impaired mechanoadaptive responses. This study highlights spatial transcriptomics as a powerful gene discovery framework for bone, enabling identification of novel targets to understand mechanisms and develop therapies.

papers.title: Neuropeptides as neuroimmune modulators in chronic wound healing: mechanistic insights and emerging therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract: Chronic wounds, typified by diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, and venous leg ulcers, represent a major clinical challenge worldwide. Persistent inflammation associated with disrupted neuroimmune crosstalk is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to impaired chronic wound healing. Neuropeptides, including substance P, calcitonin gene-related peptide, neuropeptide Y, and vasoactive intestinal peptide, act as context-dependent neuroimmune mediators that regulate immune-cell states, inflammation resolution, angiogenesis, re-epithelialization, and extracellular-matrix remodeling through partly distinct mechanisms. This review systematically examines the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which these neuropeptides influence the chronic wound microenvironment, with particular attention to their dose-, phase-, receptor-, and cell-dependent effects. Emerging therapeutic strategies are also summarized, including conventional and stimuli-responsive hydrogels, nanoparticle-hydrogel composites, hydrogel microspheres, microneedles, electrospun scaffolds, cell-based approaches, extracellular-vesicle-based combination strategies, electrical stimulation, photobiomodulation, and anti-infective combination platforms. Most of the available evidence remains preclinical. Key translational challenges include peptide instability, receptor desensitization, wound heterogeneity, delivery-system manufacturing and standardization, and peptide-specific long-term safety. Collectively, current evidence supports neuropeptide signaling as a promising but context-dependent target for precision neuroimmune modulation in chronic wound healing.

papers.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. papers.title: ROCK signaling at the interface of fibrosis and neurodegeneration: mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinases 1 and 2 (ROCK1 and ROCK2) regulate cytoskeletal dynamics, actomyosin contractility, extracellular matrix remodeling, and responses to mechanical stress. In the eye and central nervous system (CNS), these functions intersect with fibrocontractile scarring, neuronal dysfunction, impaired regeneration, and neuroinflammation. This review examines ROCK signaling at the interface of ocular fibrosis and neurodegeneration, emphasizing the retina as a setting in which neural injury and pathological remodeling can coexist. We outline the physiological and pathological consequences of ROCK-mediated mechanotransduction, using peripheral fibrosis only as brief comparative context, and examine its relationship with MRTF/SRF and YAP/TAZ transcriptional modules. We then assess evidence from ocular fibrotic disease, axonal regeneration, synaptic plasticity, microglial activation, and CNS injury-associated scarring, distinguishing direct ROCK-dependent mechanisms from extrapolation across tissues. ROCK1 and ROCK2 display overlapping functions with context-dependent specialization, but current evidence does not support a universal division of labor between the isoforms. Single-cell, spatial, and multi-omics approaches offer opportunities to identify disease-relevant cell populations, although transcript abundance alone cannot establish kinase activity or therapeutic dependence. Finally, we consider ocular and neural therapeutic development, including isoform-informed targeting, local delivery, and mechanism-aligned combinations. The central challenge is to suppress persistent pathological remodeling while preserving physiological repair and beneficial neural or glial responses. Resolving the cellular, spatial, and temporal requirements for ROCK signaling will be essential for testing whether antifibrotic and neuroprotective effects can be achieved together.

papers.title: Periostin within the tumor microenvironment: molecular insights and immunomodulatory roles in cancer.
papers.abstract: Periostin, also known as osteoblast-specific factor 2 (OSF-2), is a secreted matricellular protein with pleiotropic functions in both physiological and pathological processes. While it contributes to tissue repair, bone remodeling, and cardiovascular and respiratory homeostasis, accumulating evidence highlights its critical role in cancer progression. In diverse malignancies-including esophageal, gastric, colorectal, pancreatic, hepatocellular, ovarian, lung, breast carcinomas, and glioma-periostin is frequently overexpressed in both the stromal and epithelial compartments. Its regulation is consistently correlated with increased tumor invasiveness, advanced clinical stage, poor prognosis, and shortened patient survival. Mechanistically, periostin promotes tumor progression through multiple interconnected pathways, including the activation of NF-κB and AKT signaling, induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, stimulation of angiogenesis, and maintenance of cancer stemness. Within the tumor microenvironment, periostin-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts drive extracellular matrix remodeling, establish an immunosuppressive niche, and impede CD8+ T-cell infiltration, thereby attenuating antitumor immunity and limiting responses to immunotherapy. This review systematically summarizes the structure, expression, and multifaceted functions of periostin, with a particular focus on its immunomodulatory actions within the tumor microenvironment, and discusses its emerging potential as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: TiO2 particles induce CHIT1 and YKL-40 in human macrophages: implications for implant-associated inflammation.

papers.title: POSTN-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts: roles in the tumor microenvironment and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are among the most abundant stromal components in the tumor microenvironment and play important roles in tumor progression, metastasis, and treatment response. papers.title: Endogenous cAMP production within tissue fibroblasts is required for spontaneous fibrosis resolution

papers.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. This advancement further improves single-cell resolution analysis in spatial transcriptomics, facilitating more accurate downstream biological analyses.

papers.title: Phylospatial optimal transport for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data integration

papers.title: Lattice and Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Architectures for Dental Implants: A Scoping Review of Design, Manufacturing, and Performance.
papers.abstract: Dental implant longevity depends on both biological integration and mechanical compatibility with bone. Dense titanium and Ti-6Al-4V implants are far stiffer than peri-implant bone, a mismatch that promotes stress shielding and marginal bone loss. Architected lattice and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures, enabled by additive manufacturing (AM), lower effective stiffness and create interconnected space for bone ingrowth, vascularization, and osseointegration, yet the value of any single architecture is hard to isolate because geometry, density, material, processing, and surface state act together. Across the 28 included studies, titanium and Ti-6Al-4V dominate (19 studies, 12 of them fabricated by laser powder bed fusion), while zirconia from vat-based ceramic routes emerges as an esthetic, biologically promising alternative (six studies). The evidence remains uneven: 24 studies included simulation, 16 physical mechanical testing, 11 in vitro biology, three in vivo validation and only two a fatigue endpoint, and none reached clinical-level evidence. A lattice implant thus behaves as the combined product of its material, architecture, process, and surface; progress depends on reporting manufactured geometry, demonstrating fatigue and debris safety, and pairing in vitro with in vivo osseointegration. On the present evidence base, architecture-level statements are best read as design hypotheses and evidence trends rather than as clinically preferred configurations.

papers.title: Multiplex immunohistochemistry in multiple myeloma: principles, spatial profiling applications, and emerging frontiers in immuno-oncology.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) progression and therapeutic resistance are dictated by the bone marrow microenvironment (BMME). We then present an expanded, bone-marrow-specific horizontal comparison of mIHC against flow cytometry, mass cytometry (CyTOF), imaging mass cytometry (IMC)/multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI), and spatial transcriptomics. Building on this technical scaffold, we organize the biological and clinical applications of mIHC along the natural disease continuum-monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) → smoldering myeloma (SMM) → newly diagnosed MM (NDMM) → post-treatment residual disease → relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) → extramedullary disease (EMD)-integrating T-cell, stromal, myeloid, and NK-cell compartments together with cytokine networks, metabolic competition, and bone-remodeling signals. papers.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
papers.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution accuracy remains lacking. In our previous work, we investigated the necessary requirements for a given bulk RNA-seq dataset to satisfy the solvability conditions in NMF theory. Based on its weak solvability conditions of NMF, a new pipeline of pseudo-bulk tissue data augmented, geometric structure guided NMF model (GSNMF+) has been developed. As a semi-supervised model, it utilizes available single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data and has shown obvious improvements in scenarios where the target bulk data contain singular cellular compositions. Nevertheless, when the available scRNA-seq data are not fully consistent with the underlying cell-type-specific GEPs present in the bulk RNA-seq data, it remains a challenge that the deconvolution accuracy will significantly decrease. In this paper, we propose an iterative GSNMF algorithm to address this challenge. First, we propose a new computational algorithm for the GSNMF method (termed as the inner iteration) and provide a theoretical proof of its convergence. We then introduce an iterative process (termed as the outer iteration) to reduce potential discrepancies between available scRNA-seq and the latent cell type specific GEPs in the bulk-tissue data. The proposed methods are evaluated on both synthetic and realistic scRNA-seq data generated bulk-tissue datasets and have shown significant improvements in deconvolution accuracy, particularly in settings where the reference scRNA-seq data are inconsistent.

papers.title: Autonomous systems in oral and maxillofacial surgery: a narrative review of current applications, regulatory considerations, and medicolegal implications.
papers.abstract: Robotic and artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly described as autonomous in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS), although the operational meaning of that term varies widely across devices and procedures. AI-driven tools can segment craniomaxillofacial anatomy, identify landmarks, and generate surgical plans with accuracy comparable to expert reference standards, but their outputs are generally not linked to robotic execution in current OMS workflows. Competency standards, society guidelines, and specialty-specific consent language have not developed in parallel, possibly leaving the operating surgeon as the default bearer of risk when employing these technologies.

papers.abstract: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. papers.title: Nitric Oxide Attenuates TGF-β-Induced Myofibroblast Differentiation Through Reversible Mitochondrial Bioenergetic Reprogramming Despite Compensatory Glycolytic Activation.
papers.abstract: Fibroproliferative disorders such as hypertrophic scars and sclerotic skin diseases are characterized by excessive fibroblast activation and differentiation into contractile myofibroblasts. Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) is a central driver of this process, promoting α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression, extracellular matrix production, and increased cellular energy demand. Nitric oxide (NO) is a key regulator of mitochondrial function and cellular bioenergetics and has been reported to exert both pro- and anti-fibrotic effects depending on the cellular context. However, the mechanisms linking NO-dependent metabolic regulation to fibroblast differentiation remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that exogenous NO, delivered by the long-acting donor DETA/NO, potently suppresses TGF-β-induced myofibroblast differentiation in primary human dermal fibroblasts. DETA/NO markedly reduced α-SMA, EDA-fibronectin, and collagen I expression while simultaneously inhibiting mitochondrial respiration, ATP-linked oxidative phosphorylation, and maximal respiratory capacity. Although NO elicited a pronounced compensatory increase in glycolytic ATP production, this response failed to preserve total cellular ATP availability, resulting in a substantial reduction in overall ATP production. Importantly, these metabolic alterations were fully reversible following removal of the NO donor, indicating transient metabolic regulation rather than irreversible cellular injury. Notably, enhanced glycolytic ATP production occurred despite profound inhibition of myofibroblast differentiation, demonstrating that increased glycolytic ATP production alone is insufficient to sustain the fibrogenic phenotype when cellular ATP availability is compromised. Inhibition of soluble guanylate cyclase by ODQ failed to reverse the anti-differentiative effects of NO, indicating that canonical NO-cGMP signaling is not required for this response. Conversely, inhibition of mitochondrial ATP synthesis by oligomycin phenocopied both the metabolic and anti-differentiative effects of NO. Collectively, our findings identify NO as a reversible regulator of mitochondrial bioenergetics and fibroblast activation and demonstrate that maintenance of cellular ATP homeostasis, rather than enhanced glycolytic ATP production per se, is a critical metabolic requirement for efficient myofibroblast differentiation. Targeting cellular bioenergetics may therefore represent a promising strategy for preventing pathological fibrosis and hypertrophic scar formation.

papers.title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omics links molecular measurements to tissue architecture, but integrating spatial transcriptomics with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because the modalities differ in sampling unit, spatial resolution, data structure, and molecular-identification certainty. papers.title: Photon-Counting CT in Oral and Maxillofacial Imaging: Clinical Applications, Dose Efficiency, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) is an emerging imaging technology that combines ultra-high spatial resolution, improved dose efficiency, reduced electronic noise, and intrinsic spectral imaging. These characteristics are particularly relevant to oral and maxillofacial radiology, where accurate depiction of small osseous and dental structures is often required in the presence of metallic restorations or implants. This review summarizes the technical principles of PCCT and examines its current and potential clinical applications across dental and maxillofacial imaging. Available evidence indicates that PCCT can improve visualization of fine root canal anatomy, periodontal and trabecular bone structures, peri-implant interfaces, subtle maxillofacial fractures, and complex sinonasal anatomy. Its spectral capabilities, including virtual monoenergetic imaging and material decomposition, may substantially reduce metal-related artifacts and improve tissue characterization. Early studies also suggest that PCCT can provide high diagnostic image quality at reduced radiation dose, with potential advantages in pediatric imaging and in patients requiring repeated examinations. Beyond morphology, PCCT may support quantitative applications such as bone mineral density assessment, iodine mapping, treatment planning, and the development of imaging biomarkers and artificial intelligence-based analysis. Despite these promising findings, cone-beam CT remains the preferred modality for many routine dental indications because of its accessibility, lower cost, and established clinical workflow. Current evidence for PCCT in oral and maxillofacial radiology is still limited and is largely derived from technical, experimental, and early clinical studies. Further prospective comparisons with cone-beam CT and conventional CT are needed to define task-specific diagnostic benefits, optimized protocols, radiation-dose advantages, and cost-effectiveness. PCCT is therefore best regarded as a promising complementary modality with particular value in diagnostically challenging cases that require very high spatial resolution, spectral information, or effective metal-artifact reduction. Nevertheless, most oral and maxillofacial evidence remains exploratory; improved image-quality metrics should not be equated with superior patient-level diagnostic accuracy. Direct comparisons with optimized CBCT yield heterogeneous, protocol-dependent dose and diagnostic findings. No standardized indication-specific PCCT acquisition framework currently exists for routine oral and maxillofacial imaging. Clinical implementation should therefore be conditional on demonstrable diagnostic benefit at a justified radiation dose and acceptable resource cost.

In breast cancer, particularly triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), the presence and maturation of TLSs have been associated with prognosis and treatment response; however, heterogeneity in TLS definition, maturation criteria, spatial sampling, and analytical platforms currently limits standardization and routine clinical implementation.Main bodyConventional histopathology provides structural information but limited molecular resolution, whereas single-cell RNA sequencing loses the spatial context that is central to TLS organization. High-resolution spatial and multi-omics technologies can partly bridge these gaps by characterizing TLS cellular composition, molecular interactions, and tissue architecture in situ. This review summarizes the biological features, histopathological classification, multi-omics characterization, clinical associations, and emerging therapeutic strategies related to TLSs in breast cancer, with particular attention to methodological limitations and translational barriers.ConclusionMore precise characterization of TLSs may inform future biomarker development and therapeutic strategies in breast cancer. Prospective validation, standardized assessment, and demonstration of incremental clinical utility are required before TLS-based approaches can be incorporated into routine clinical decision-making.

papers.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHead and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.MethodsSingle-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from three HNSCC cohorts were integrated with TCGA-HNSC and five GEO cohorts. Epithelial-state heterogeneity, inferred trajectories, regulons, cell-cell communication, prognostic features, spatial localization, and ferroptosis-associated transcriptional programs were analyzed. SLC5A12 was prioritized through convergent computational analyses and was subsequently tested by loss-of-function assays and xenograft experiments. CellOracle perturbation, ferroptosis-related drug-sensitivity analyses, and molecular docking were treated as computational predictions.ResultsFive epithelial states were identified, among which the Invasive population increased with disease progression and exhibited the highest inferred CNV burden. Invasive cells showed enrichment of malignant and extracellular-matrix programs and prominent predicted MIF-CD74/CXCR4 communication with regulatory T cells. Machine-learning, WGCNA, single-cell, and spatial analyses converged on SLC5A12 as an Invasive-state-associated prognostic feature. Computational analyses further indicated a ferroptosis-associated vulnerability profile in the Invasive state and predicted attenuation of invasive and immunoregulatory programs after virtual SLC5A12 loss. Experimentally, SLC5A12 knockdown reduced proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth while increasing apoptosis. Structure-based virtual screening nominated ledipasvir (ZINC000150338819) and elbasvir (ZINC000150588351) as top-ranked candidate SLC5A12-binding compounds.ConclusionSLC5A12 is a molecular feature of an Invasive epithelial state associated with HNSCC progression, adverse outcome, and predicted immune-remodeling and therapeutic-vulnerability programs. Experimental loss-of-function data support a tumor-promoting role for SLC5A12, whereas the MIF-Treg communication, ferroptosis vulnerability, CellOracle perturbation, and molecular-docking findings remain computational hypotheses requiring direct validation.

papers.title: Efficient Powder Removal and Micro-Nano Structural Formation in 3D-Printed Porous Titanium Implants for Enhanced Osteogenesis.
papers.abstract: Powder bed fusion-laser beam enables the fabrication of patient-specific medical implants; however, the complete removal of residual powders from complex porous architectures remains a major challenge, compromising biological performance. In this study, a high-voltage (90 V) anodic oxidation (AO) surface polishing strategy was developed to achieve efficient powder removal and surface optimization of triply periodic minimal surface gyroid porous titanium implants. AO treatment markedly reduced surface roughness, slightly enlarged the pore size by approximately 30 to 50 μm while maintaining an overall pore size of 300 to 600 μm, and generated a honeycomb-like microstructure favorable for cell adhesion and bone ingrowth. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis confirmed the formation of a stable and compact TiO2 film, which enhanced hydrophilicity and negative surface charge, thereby promoting calcium phosphate deposition and osteogenic mineralization. Both in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated significantly improved early-stage cell adhesion, long-term mineralization, and bone regeneration after AO treatment compared with untreated controls. Polished CP-Ti-AU-45 specimens achieved a new bone mineral density of 0.19 g/cm3 and a bone volume fraction of 33.8%. The molecular mechanism may involve the activation of extracellular matrix-receptor interactions, adhesion plaques, and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways while inhibiting ferroptosis-related signaling pathways, leading to a significant increase in the messenger RNA levels of Runx2 and Mef2c. The AO polishing strategy preserved the mechanical integrity of porous metals while integrating efficient powder removal with surface functionalization, thereby substantially enhancing the osseointegration potential of porous metallic implants.

papers.title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
papers.abstract: Introduction: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve compartment-specific molecular programs in kidney disease, but its cost and technical requirements limit its use in clinical diagnostics and in large biopsy archives. Predicting spatial gene expression from routine histology with artificial intelligence could extend molecular characterization to existing clinically annotated kidney tissue collections. Methods: We adapted DeepSpot-M, a pretrained multimodal foundation model that predicts spatial gene expression from histology, using paired hematoxylin and eosin images and Visium spatial transcriptomics from 209 Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP) participants. We evaluated virtual profiles in held-out human biopsies, associated them with histopathologic and biochemical injury markers in 567 rats with defined nephrotoxin exposures from a public toxicogenomics database, and generated a virtual atlas from 1,534 histology slides of 476 additional KPMP participants. Results: Kidney-specific adaptation of DeepSpot-M doubled the mean Pearson correlation of each model's 1,000 best-predicted genes (0.43 versus 0.22) and exceeded recent foundation models. Virtual profiles preserved the direction of all 13 disease-marker differences in measured expression, including tubular injury, maladaptive repair, gluconeogenesis, and fibrosis-associated programs. All 11 measured associations between molecular programs and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were also preserved. Without rat-specific training, a virtual injury score distinguished moderate or severe histopathologic lesions (area under the curve, 0.85) and at least twofold blood urea nitrogen elevation (0.82). In our atlas of 5.46 million virtual spots, higher proximal tubule program scores were associated with higher eGFR (partial r, 0.32) and less interstitial fibrosis (-0.57), and program-pathology associations agreed with those of measured Visium profiles in independent participants (Spearman rho, 0.64). Conclusions: Kidney-adapted virtual spatial transcriptomics links histology-derived molecular programs to experimental renal injury and human clinical and histologic phenotypes. Our approach enables spatial molecular analyses in routine biopsy histology, which could help decipher disease-associated pathways in existing biopsy archives.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Identify CDKN2A as a Ferroptosis-Related Regulator of 5-Fluorouracil Resistance in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment. Ferroptosis has emerged as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors, but its role in CRC chemotherapy resistance remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated bulk transcriptomic, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic, and experimental analyses to identify ferroptosis-related determinants of chemotherapy resistance in CRC. Transcriptomic analysis identified 28 chemotherapy resistance-related ferroptosis genes. Single-cell analysis showed that malignant epithelial cells had lower Chemotherapy Resistance Ferroptosis Scores (CRFscores) than normal epithelial cells, while CRFscore-low malignant cells exhibited enhanced metabolic activity and tumor-promoting pathway features. CDKN2A emerged as a key candidate associated with unfavorable chemotherapy outcomes, reduced ferroptosis-related activity, and stronger spatial associations with myeloid populations. Functional validation in HCT116/5-FU and HCT8/5-FU cells showed that CDKN2A was upregulated in resistant cells, whereas CDKN2A depletion enhanced 5-FU sensitivity and reduced clonogenic survival. CDKN2A knockdown also increased lipid ROS, intracellular labile iron, and malondialdehyde accumulation, while ferrostatin-1 partially reversed these effects. Moreover, CDKN2A depletion reduced PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and decreased SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression. Collectively, our findings identify CDKN2A as a potential regulator linking ferroptosis resistance to 5-FU resistance in CRC and suggest that CDKN2A-associated ferroptosis resistance may represent a therapeutic vulnerability for overcoming chemotherapy resistance.

papers.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
papers.abstract: Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability. Results: We present ARC-Impute, which regularises cell-to-spot mapping through anchor-residual optimisation, target-guided reference curation and routing, and twin-panel consistency. Across 17 human and mouse datasets spanning spot-based and single-cell technologies, ARC-Impute ranked first for held-out Pearson correlation throughout and exceeded the dataset-specific baseline mean by 47.3% on average. It also achieved the strongest spot-level cell-type composition recovery across three pseudospot benchmarks and retained leading accuracy and consistency under reference and training-gene perturbations. Cross-validated predictions revealed systematic differences in gene imputability. Availability and implementation: Code and workflows at https://github.com/ethanhaan/arc-impute.

papers.title: Spatial single cell multi-omics identifies divergent melanoma-cell states associated with metastatic outcomes in thin primary melanomas
papers.abstract: Thin melanomas (Breslow thickness ≤1 mm) generally have favorable outcomes, yet some metastasise, highlighting the need for biomarkers of progression. Here, we combined same-section single-cell spatial transcriptomics and proteomics to identify seven melanoma-cell states organized along two inferred trajectories sharing a common trunk, extending from an in situ epithelial-adjacent state through developmental stress to melanocytic differentiation before diverging into two lineages. Lineage 1 progressed through an IFN-associated stress intermediate state towards mesenchymal-invasive cells enriched in metastasizing tumors and associated with immune-hot neighborhoods, extracellular-matrix remodeling and angiogenesis, potentially supporting vascular mimicry and metastatic dissemination. Lineage 2 terminated in cohesive nevus-like cells retaining melanocytic features within relatively immune-cold neighborhoods and enriched in non-metastasizing tumors. We confirmed these associations using H&E-inferred spatial transcriptomics in an international multicentric cohort and independent bulk transcriptomic datasets in primary melanomas, linking spatially organized melanoma-cell programs to metastatic outcome and identifying potential biomarkers of progression in thin melanoma.

papers.title: PDAC BioPortal: An Integrated Web Resource for Multi-Scale Analysis of Pancreatic Cancer Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound cellular heterogeneity and treatment-associated remodeling, yet bulk, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomic datasets remain fragmented across separate portals. papers.title: The STP Open Challenge: A Community Effort to Define and Benchmark Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract While spatial transcriptomics technologies are increasingly accessible, spatial proteomics remains constrained by high costs and limited throughput. Furthermore, poor mRNA-protein correlation, driven by post-transcriptional regulation, necessitates multi-omics integration for complementary biological insights. Current RNA-to-protein prediction models, primarily trained on bulk or single-cell data, often overlook critical spatial context. Consequently, it remains unclear which model architecture, spatial representation, or histopathological features best facilitate spatial protein abundance inference. To address these gaps, we defined the STP (Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome) task and launched the STP Open Challenge, a competition for predicting spatial proteomics from spatial transcriptomics of adjacent tissue sections. Utilizing a curated paired spatial dataset and a standardized evaluation framework, the challenge attracted 101 teams and yielded 896 valid submissions. Top-performing methods achieved strong predictive performance while preserving spatial organization. The landscape of submitted models revealed diverse modeling strategies and motivated us to develop a consensus-based ensemble framework that leverages various participant methods to enhance prediction robustness. Extended evaluation on unseen datasets demonstrated that the top-performing models outperformed existing baselines, highlighting the effectiveness of the community effort for this task. By formally defining the STP task and providing a standardized benchmarking platform, this work establishes a foundation for scalable, cost-effective spatial proteomics prediction and future multi-omics integration.

papers.title: Spatial organization of a SPINK1-associated tumor-stromal ecosystem links metabolic remodeling to immune restriction in bladder cancer
papers.abstract: Spatially organized tumor-stromal interactions contribute to metabolic remodeling and immune suppression in bladder cancer (BLCA). Using spatial transcriptional programs to define single-cell states, we identified a niche comprising SPINK1-high epithelial cells (E2) and TPM2-high cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) (C1). SPINK1 promoted tumor growth and myofibroblastic CAF programs, with EGFR and TGF-{beta} signaling implicated in tumor-CAF communication. Inferred metabolic reactions and spatial metabolite distributions supported a candidate circuit linking tumor-derived lactate to CAF oxidative metabolism and glutamine provision, followed by tumor glutamine utilization for reductive carboxylation and fatty acid synthesis. SPINK1 perturbation altered extracellular glutamine and lactate concentrations. Predicted chemokine interactions implicated C2/C3 CAFs in T cell recruitment, whereas the E2-C1 niche exhibited checkpoint and exhaustion-associated features. RHCG-positive tumor regions contained higher proportions of TOXCXCR4 cells among CD3 T cells, suggesting a possible association between ammonia handling and T cell dysfunction. In vivo, Spink1 loss attenuated tumor progression, increased cytotoxic CD8 T-cell infiltration, and enhanced tumor control during PD-1 blockade. These findings identify a spatially organized tumor-stromal niche associated with metabolic cooperation and immune restriction, supporting SPINK1 as a candidate therapeutic target in combination with immunotherapy.

papers.title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
papers.abstract: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations. Peak lactation is characterized by expansion of luminal alveolar cells and increased {beta}-casein and -lactalbumin expression, whereas luminal progenitors, hormone-sensing cells, fibroblasts, and B cells are enriched in the dry period. Trajectory inference place luminal progenitors near branches toward alveolar and hormone-sensing states, with sustained ELF5-associated activity along the alveolar branch. Myoepithelial, macrophage, natural killer T, and T cell states are also remodeled. SPP1 and MIF signaling networks become more connected and change their cellular targets. These data establish a period resolved atlas of dairy goat mammary remodeling and identify coordinated epithelial, stromal, immune, and communication programs associated with active lactation.

papers.title: RAD: A Read-structure Agnostic Demultiplexer for Single-Cell Long-Read Sequencing and Analysis
papers.abstract: Single-cell long-read sequencing (LRS) techniques enable the analysis of full transcript sequences within a cell. However, LRS introduces computational challenges for parsing information, often necessitating the development of custom workflows to handle complex read layouts, such as split combinatorial barcodes. To address these challenges, we introduce an error-robust, read-structure agnostic demultiplexer (RAD). In RAD, users can easily specify read structure, such as adapter sequence and relative barcode position, and can rapidly extract these elements for each read. RAD implements highly accurate barcode whitelist generation from long-read data alone, without the benefit of short-read support or priors while uniquely avoiding common but previously uncharacterized errors during demultiplexing. RAD's comprehensive barcode error correction protocols allow for more sensitive and precise barcode-read assignments. In synthetic and real-world benchmarks against gold-standard demultiplexers, RAD is faster and achieves better biological discovery capability in downstream gene expression analysis than existing pipelines. We show RAD can be applied to datasets ranging from high-definition long-read spatial transcriptomics to targeted long-read single-cell immune receptor sequencing, making it a powerful and scalable tool for both standard and custom long-read sequencing experiments.

papers.title: Loss of contractile arteriolar smooth muscle cells and their GLP1R expression in human diabetic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists slow kidney disease progression in type 2 diabetes, and in the human kidney the receptor is localized mainly to arteriolar smooth muscle. Whether these cells and their receptor are preserved in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is unknown. We combined single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics of 5,101 genes with registered periodic acid-Schiff histology in kidney biopsies from 28 people with DKD, 102 with other glomerular diseases and 24 living donors, and measured 2,531 arterioles and small arteries. Arteriolar walls in DKD contained about 20% fewer smooth muscle cells than those in other glomerular diseases, and the loss fell on cells without matrix gene expression. Transcripts of GLP1R, which encodes the receptor, were detected in 0.48% of the remaining smooth muscle cells in DKD, compared with 1.21% in other glomerular diseases and 1.75% in donors. The glutamate receptor gene GRIA2 and the smooth muscle regulator PRDM6 were also lower, whereas contractile genes were unchanged, a pattern not seen in the other diseases. In an independent single-nucleus atlas, smooth muscle GLP1R was lower in DKD than in reference kidneys, and smooth muscle content fell with arteriolar hyalinosis grade. In human DKD, arterioles lose contractile smooth muscle cells, and fewer of the remaining cells carry transcripts for the receptor targeted by GLP-1 receptor agonists at the disease stage in which these drugs are used.
