papers.title: LUCID: joint cell typing and neighbour-aware decontamination of segmented spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Cell profiles in segmented spatial transcriptomics are contaminated by RNA of neighbouring cells and by segmentation errors that merge two cells. LUCID is a multinomial mixture model that jointly assigns a type to each cell, tests whether its profile mixes two types and estimates the fraction of counts coming from its neighbours. An external reference is adapted to the platform, an identifiability rule protects a cell's own signal and the test is calibrated by parametric bootstrap. LUCID works with or without a reference, runs on CPUs and returns integer counts for all genes. On three public Visium HD datasets (mouse brain, human colorectal cancer, mouse liver) and in simulations built on them, LUCID removed contamination from other cell types as well as a two-step baseline, flagged fewer contaminated cells as mixed, emptied no cell and preserved minority lineages where one cell type dominates.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
papers.abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A, respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.

papers.title: Obesity remodels the testicular microenvironment: Spatial transcriptomics identifies local IGF dysregulation associated with spermatogenic failure
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Obesity is a global metabolic disorder strongly associated with male infertility, but the spatial and molecular mechanisms underlying testicular dysfunction remain unclear. Methods We combined single-cell and high-definition spatial transcriptomics to construct an integrated spatial atlas of the cynomolgus monkey testis in both normal and obese conditions. Results This approach revealed a previously unrecognized spatial misdirection of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) signaling in the obese testicular microenvironment. Concurrently, the IGF1 receptor and IGF2 receptor were enriched in adjacent somatic cells, suggesting a localized autocrine and paracrine signaling hub. These spatially restricted IGF-associated changes accompanied macrophage expansion and inflammatory polarization, increased myoid cell abundance, and basement membrane remodeling. The ensuing chronic inflammatory niche directly correlated with down-regulation of blood-testis barrier genes including CLDN11 and TJP1, with protein-level validation for CLDN11 and GATA4. Spermatogenesis was broadly impaired, with stage-specific transcriptional programs attenuated across the germline and ferroptosis-related gene set scores selectively increased in spermatogonia. Conclusions Our findings link spatially compartmentalized IGF dysregulation to testicular inflammation and spermatogenic impairment in obesity, highlighting IGF1, IGFBP5, and IGFBP7 as candidate mediators and providing a molecular basis for future research on obesity-associated male reproductive dysfunction.

papers.title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
papers.abstract: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. papers.title: Identifying disease-associated dysbiosis in image-based spatial microbiome via MiSA
papers.abstract: Background: Extensive studies have revealed the associations of microbiome dysbiosis with disease through compositional analysis of 16S rRNA amplicon or shotgun metagenomic sequencing data. However, dysbiosis in spatial organization of microbiome inhabiting the body sites and its implication for diseases remain understudied. Recently developed high phylogenetic resolution fluorescence in situ hybridization (HiPR-FISH) is an image-based mapping technology that provides spatial microbiome data at single-cell resolution, which allows for visualizing and quantifying spatial arrangement of microbial cells. Despite the growing availability of such data, no methods have been tailored to studying spatial dysbiosis in image-based microbiome data. Results: Here we introduce MiSA (Microbiome Spatial Aberration), the first statistical framework for identifying disease-associated spatial dysbiosis and the individual taxa that may contribute to it, based on differing degrees of clustering or regularity, i.e., microbial cells being more aggregated or more evenly spaced than expected under complete spatial randomness, between diagnostic groups. In simulations based on a real dataset, MiSA was robust across diverse and noisy spatial configurations, achieving substantially higher statistical power than a method borrowed from spatial proteomics, while controlling type I error at both the individual-taxon and community levels. When applied to an oral biofilm study, MiSA detected peri-implant mucositis-associated spatial dysbiosis at the community level and identified five taxa as potential contributors, including Actinomyces, which showed increased clustering in mucositis. Conclusions: MiSA is a powerful and robust framework for identifying spatial dysbiosis and the contributing taxa in image-based microbiome data, offering new insights into the spatial organization of microbial communities in disease.

papers.title: Homeostatic fibroblast niche collapse in clinically uninvolved skin defines a subclinical state of systemic sclerosis
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, or scleroderma, is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Heterogeneous clinical presentation and polygenic risk complicate our understanding of disease mechanisms and the path to effective therapy. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses have revealed substantial heterogeneity in skin, but disease-associated reprogramming remains poorly defined. To address this, we performed high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiling of paired clinically uninvolved and clinically affected scleroderma donor skin alongside healthy controls. We identified a continuum of cellular, molecular, and spatial changes to the stroma that were already evident in clinically uninvolved tissue yet remained distinct from the more extensive changes in paired fibrotic biopsies. Uninvolved skin was comparable to healthy tissue by clinical and histopathological assessment, but distinguishable by the proportional reduction, transcriptional reprogramming, and spatial isolation of LGR5+SCARA5+PI16+ progenitor fibroblasts. In parallel, the dermal vascular smooth muscle compartment shifted from a contractile to a synthetic, activated state, suggesting dysfunctional vascular reprogramming occurs in the absence of overt fibrosis. Cell neighborhood analysis revealed that progenitor fibroblasts occupy dense stromal niches in healthy skin that collapse in clinically uninvolved tissue, replaced by isolated, disease-associated fibroblast populations. These data indicate that clinically uninvolved skin occupies an intermediate subclinical state of scleroderma, establishing a framework for strategies to allow early diagnosis and preserve homeostatic fibroblast niches to prevent irreversible tissue remodeling and fibrotic commitment.

papers.title: Breastfeeding Enables Systemic Transfer of Functional Maternal Immune Cells to Neonates
papers.abstract: Does breastfeeding transfer living maternal immune cells that persist and function in offspring, beyond providing soluble immune factors? Using a foster-nursing mouse model that eliminates prenatal exposure, this study directly tests whether maternal cells can be transferred postnatally through breastmilk. Single-cell RNA sequencing shows that transferred cells span multiple hematopoietic lineages, dominated by monocyte-derived macrophages with a distinct stress-adapted, inflammatory transcriptional state compatible with persistence in the neonatal environment. Our findings suggest that breastfeeding may serve as a postnatal route for maternal cellular transfer, potentially extending maternal immune influence beyond gestation.

papers.title: Cell-type-resolved methylation analysis using bulk long-read sequencing across human tissues
papers.abstract: DNA methylation shapes cellular identity and changes with aging and disease, but most human methylomes come from bulk tissue, which mixes signal across many cell types. A methylation change at the bulk tissue level can reflect a change in cellular composition or an intrinsic shift within a cell type, and the two cannot be separated from bulk data. Single-cell and sorted-cell methods resolve cell types directly, but their cost and workflow complexity pose challenges to large studies. Long-read sequencing of single DNA molecules can directly detect DNA methylation on each read. We built COMET (Cell-of-Origin from METhylation), a framework that uses cell-type-specific methylation to assign individual long reads to cell types from standard bulk long-read sequencing. COMET detects changes in cell-type composition robustly even from shallow bulk long-read data, quantifies methylation level of repetitive DNA within each cell type, and, with deeper sequencing, resolves methylation differences between health and disease in individual cell types. We applied COMET to 140 human blood samples, 104 human brain samples and 59 human colon samples. In blood, we found epigenetic aging clock is primarily driven by shifts in cell-type composition, and that APOE4 carriers have myeloid-specific methylation changes. In brain, we found sex-biased change in cell-type composition with age, resolved methylation and hydroxymethylation separately within each cell type. In colon, we found a consistent expansion of fibroblasts in tumors relative to matched normal tissue, localized methylation loss at LINE-1 in fibroblast cells, and identified tumor- and cell-type-specific hypermethylation in epithelial cells at the promoters of known colorectal cancer genes. By resolving cell-type-specific methylation directly from bulk long-read data, this approach opens broad study of cell-type epigenetics across human tissues in aging and disease.

papers.title: Switch from inflammatory signaling to excessive extracellular matrix remodeling in fibrotic fibroblasts attenuates monocyte tissue infiltration
papers.abstract: Tissue damage induces infiltration of monocytes that differentiate into macrophages and cooperate with fibroblasts in tissue repair. If repair fails and tissue stress persists, a feedforward loop involving high contractility of activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, and TGF-{beta}1 signaling can lead to chronic fibrosis characterized by hypertrophic scarring. This did not affect overall fibroblast-stimulated monocyte migration through the ECM, but it prevented monocytes from crossing liquid-hydrogel barriers to penetrate the collagen network. Moreover, it caused excessive ECM remodeling near clusters of fibroblasts, which locally arrested monocyte migration. These findings indicate that excessive fibroblast activation in fibrotic tissues can shift the balance from chemotactic cues toward biomechanical constraints, which limits monocyte infiltration and locally restricts monocyte migration.

papers.title: Spatial causal discovery reveals novel mechanisms of cellular senescence in human liver
papers.abstract: The complex network of mechanisms that surround cellular senescence, such as its precise causes and effects, are not entirely understood at present. Senescence occurs when a cell permanently ceases dividing, halts apoptosis, stops performing its normal functions, and begins secreting chemicals that can induce other cells in its environment to also become senescent. Senescent cells are present in both healthy and unhealthy tissue, but their abundance is positively correlated with disease and age. A better understanding of senescence could lead to healthier aging, improved recovery from chemotherapy, or increased lifespan. This study used novel machine learning algorithms - with guaranteed properties of correctness under broad assumptions - to investigate senescence in human liver tissue by analyzing Visium spatial transcriptomics data. This produced data-driven models of the causes and effects of senescence, both locally and from nearby tissue. This report includes an assessment of whether the data meet key requirements for causal analysis, the transcripts identified by causal analyses as causes and effects of senescence marker genes, and pathway analyses of those gene sets. We show that Visium data from human liver tissue satisfies the causal Markov condition. 3. We introduce novel spatial extensions of established causal discovery machine learning algorithms and apply them on Visium data from human liver tissue. The causal modeling produced lists of transcripts directly (i) upstream and (ii) downstream of senescence marker genes, which had relatively little overlap with standard senescence marker lists SenMayo and SenUMN. 4. Pathway analyses of the upstream and downstream transcripts reveal that senescence-associated signaling integrates cellular stress inputs and immune responses to fuel a self-sustaining loop of integrin-mediated TGF-β activation and continuous matrix deposition.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Cutaneous melanoma remains the deadliest skin cancer despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. EGFR was the only risk-factor gene (coefficient = +0.118); the remaining genes were protective. It stratifies survival in TCGA-SKCM, is independent of stage, captures an immune-cold phenotype concordant with spatial findings, and is directionally consistent in external cohorts. These findings generate testable hypotheses for selecting patients for EGFR inhibitor and immunotherapy combinations and provide a bulk-computable biomarker for prospective testing. The signature is not yet a validated clinical assay, but it is a biologically anchored, hypothesis generating tool that operationalizes the EGFR-driven, immune-cold phenotype and is immediately testable in existing RNA-seq cohorts.

papers.abstract: Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics (SST) offers unprecedented opportunities to decipher tissue architecture at subcellular resolution. papers.title: Light-based therapies in dentistry: applications in cariology, endodontics, and periodontology.
papers.abstract: Light-based therapies are increasingly used in dentistry as adjunctive and minimally invasive tools. They support diagnosis, microbial reduction, tissue modulation, pain control and healing. This mini review summarizes their applications in cariology, endodontics and periodontology. The main modalities include dental lasers, antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, photoactivated disinfection and photobiomodulation. In cariology, light-based therapies assist in caries detection, selective caries removal, bacterial reduction, enamel and dentin modification, remineralisation support and dentin hypersensitivity management. However, most data are derived from in vitro or short-term clinical studies, and their long-term benefits over conventional preventive and restorative care remain unclear. In endodontics, laser-assisted irrigation and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy may improve root canal disinfection and biofilm disruption and may be helpful in managing persistent infections. However, differences in wavelengths, power settings, photosensitizers and clinical protocols limit standardisation. In periodontology, light-based therapies have been studied as adjuncts to scaling and root planing, peri-implant disease treatment, postoperative pain control and soft-tissue healing. Current evidence suggests short-term reductions in inflammation and microbial load, but clinical outcomes remain variable. Important limitations include unclear indications, variable dosimetry, thermal safety concerns, high cost and limited long-term clinical evidence. Standardised protocols and high-quality randomised clinical trials are needed. Future progress will depend on precise dosimetry, device standardisation, and improved understanding of light-tissue-microbe interactions. Overall, light-based therapies show promising potential in dentistry, with existing literature supporting their various applications and effects; however, substantial heterogeneity in study designs and treatment parameters precludes standardised recommendations.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics in hematological malignancies: from cellular neighborhoods to the architecture of tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: In 2020, Nature announced spatially resolved transcriptomics as "Method of the Year." Therefore, the next step toward precision medicine could be to use these insights to guide more spatially informed treatment.We reviewed spatial transcriptomics technologies, their applications in hematological malignancies, the challenges of these cutting-edge approaches, and future perspectives.

papers.title: Clinical applications of artificial intelligence in oral and maxillofacial surgery: a scoping review mapping the evidence and evaluation practices.
papers.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS), and yet the scope of its clinical applications and the methodological practices used to evaluate them remain incompletely characterized. Of 3760 unique records screened, 1496 studies were included. Annual output rose from 59 studies in 2020 to 407 in 2025, and 64.0% of the corpus was published from 2024 onward. Evidence was unevenly distributed: oral and maxillofacial pathology and oncology accounted for 623 studies (41.6%), more than the next three domains combined, while the four smallest domains together accounted for 203 (13.6%). Charted AI tasks were grouped into nine task families, the largest being detection and diagnostic classification (612 studies) and segmentation and landmarking (272); a single task-and-domain combination, detection within pathology and oncology, accounted for more studies than any other complete family. Retrospectively collected data predominated (1161 studies, 77.6%). A five-indicator Methodological Quality Profile, applied uniformly and reported as a descriptive record of what studies reported rather than as a risk-of-bias assessment, recorded external validation in 156 studies (10.4%), a prospective or randomized design in 63 (4.2%), and a direct AI-versus-clinician comparison in 246 (16.4%), with no directional change in any of these across the review period; 1081 studies (72.3%) recorded none of the three. Output in OMFS AI has grown rapidly without a corresponding change in evaluation practice.

papers.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in cellular-resolution biology, including single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial omics, and multimodal molecular profiling, together with computational systems biology, enable increasingly detailed characterization of cellular states, spatial organization, and molecular relationships within the ovarian-follicular environment. In this Review, we use the ovarian cellular ecosystem as an operational systems framework to test whether PCOS-associated abnormalities observed in individual ovarian and follicular compartments form reproducible higher-order patterns of multicellular organization. The framework is organized across five measurable domains: cellular composition and states, intercellular signaling relationships, spatial niche organization, cross-compartment molecular coupling, and systemic-ovarian coupling. Current direct human cellular-resolution evidence remains sparse and compartment-specific. Available studies support altered molecular and cellular states within selected ovarian and follicular compartments more strongly than coordinated, spatially organized, or progressive ecosystem-wide remodeling. To validate our method, we contribute ImplantFairy, the first large-scale public dataset for dental implant planning, comprising 1,622 implant-specific CBCT samples. papers.title: From Passive Matrices to Bioresponsive Interfaces: Polymer-Based Biomaterials for Oral Soft Tissue Augmentation.
papers.abstract: Soft tissue deficiencies around teeth and dental implants remain a common clinical challenge affecting aesthetics, tissue stability, and long-term maintenance. papers.title: Fibrotic Scars and the Potential Therapeutics After Spinal Cord Injury.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) affects millions of people worldwide, resulting in persistent direct and secondary effects including but not limited to motor, sensory, and autonomic dysfunction. The widespread nature of this condition, as well as its detrimental effects, makes recovery following SCI an important clinical problem. One primary issue identified in SCI among other neurological conditions is fibrotic scarring, as its dynamic nature provides both beneficial and detrimental effects over its developmental course. Initially, early scar formation contributes to wound closure and tissue stabilization, but chronic, persistent fibrosis later interferes with axonal growth and other neural repair mechanisms. The scar itself is highly dynamic, consisting of components including collagens, fibronectin, proteoglycans, and laminins, all of which have diverse localization and functionality throughout scar maturation. Its formation is regulated by various signaling mechanisms, including inflammatory signaling, profibrotic pathways, vascular responses, interactions between fibroblasts and neighboring cells, and changes in the specific mechanical environment of the injury site. This review focuses primarily on SCI, with findings from additional central nervous system injury and disease models used to provide a holistic, clinically relevant overview of fibrotic scar organization, profibrotic signaling, and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiac Fibrosis: Genomic and Molecular Drivers, Emerging Biomarkers and Therapeutic Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Chronically elevated angiotensin II (Ang II) drives adverse cardiac remodelling, converting a reparative response into progressive interstitial and perivascular fibrosis that stiffens the ventricle and precedes overt heart failure. We then consider why fibrosis regression under RAAS blockade appears heterogeneous, which emerging targets are mechanistically credible, and how genotype-biomarker-imaging phenotyping could enrich antifibrotic trials. Priorities for ancestrally diverse cohorts and standardised biomarker methodology are identified.

papers.title: The Immunological Biography of the Carotid Plaque: From Trained Immunity and Clonal Lymphocytes to Spatial Immune Niches and Plaque Vulnerability.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic carotid plaques are shaped by years of interaction between systemic risk factors, hematopoietic conditioning, vascular injury, and local immune responses, yet conventional assessment captures only a limited snapshot of this biological history. We propose the Carotid Plaque Immune Phenotype (CPIP) as an integrative framework linking systemic immune history with cellular state, clonal architecture, spatial organization, and clinically relevant plaque features. Combining circulating biomarkers with tissue-resolved immune profiling may ultimately improve biological phenotyping of carotid atherosclerosis and provide a framework for prospective studies linking plaque immune architecture with cerebrovascular events.

papers.title: The role of cellular signaling pathways in the therapeutic effects of sonodynamic therapy against periodontitis: A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dysbiotic subgingival biofilms and driven by a dysregulated host response that destroys the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone. Mechanical debridement remains the cornerstone of therapy, but biofilm tolerance, anatomically inaccessible niches, and the limited action of antimicrobials on host-mediated tissue destruction leave clinically relevant gaps. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses low-intensity ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers and generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), offering deeper tissue reach than light-based approaches and a route to site-specific, non-antibiotic adjunctive care. Beyond microbial killing, ROS and co-released mediators may reshape host signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on signaling pathways modulated by SDT and grades it by proximity to periodontitis. Direct evidence from periodontal or jawbone-infection studies concerns NF-κB, NLRP3/caspase-1, Toll-like receptor (TLR) and NOD-like receptor signaling, IL-17 signaling, osteoclast differentiation, M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, and AMPK and PI3K/Akt-associated osteogenesis. Mechanistic precedents from non-periodontal models concern ROS-PPARγ-NF-κB, Nrf2/ARE, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-autophagy signaling. Direct periodontal evidence is limited to a small number of preclinical studies, pathway-level claims rest mainly on transcript- or protein-level associations, and the anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic effects of some platforms are attributable to co-delivered nitric oxide or metal ions rather than to sonodynamic ROS. We therefore distinguish SDT-dependent from platform-dependent effects, discuss dental translational issues (delivery, ultrasound source and dosimetry, safety, peri-implantitis, systemic comorbidity), and propose research priorities: pathway-specific validation, standardized ultrasound reporting, and controlled clinical trials of SDT as an adjunct to subgingival instrumentation.

papers.title: Elasticity per Thickness Index for Breast Sonoelastography: Quantitative Analysis of Implant- and Clinically Related Peri-Implant Capsular Formation.
papers.abstract: Background: Peri-implant capsular formation remains a multifactorial process influenced by implant characteristics and patient-specific tissue responses. papers.title: Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Fields Combined with Triamcinolone Acetonide for Hypertrophic Scar Treatment: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HS) is a common fibrotic disorder following wound healing for which no universally effective therapy currently exists. papers.title: Wound atlas of Atlantic salmon skin.
papers.abstract: The process of wound healing offers a window into how cells coordinate to maintain tissue integrity, repair damage, and restore tissue function. papers.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies.
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. From signaling, we move to the pathways behind infection-driven osteogenic suppression: the core signaling pathways through which bacterial virulence factors suppress osteogenesis, including TLR-mediated NF-κB activation, RANKL/OPG imbalance-driven osteoclastogenesis, and biofilm hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming. We then look at how macrophages (M1/M2 polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome), neutrophils (NETosis), and T cells shape the host response to infection and bone repair. We close with current synergistic design strategies-metal ion doping, antimicrobial peptide loading, organic-inorganic composite coatings, temporally controlled drug release-and next-generation smart responsive surfaces including pH-responsive, photothermal/photocatalytic, enzyme-responsive, and immunomodulatory coatings. This review aims to provide a mechanistic framework for understanding infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TNT surfaces and to guide the rational design of dual-functional implants that simultaneously combat infection and promote bone regeneration.

papers.title: The Role of Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Lung Cancer Progression and Therapy: From Mechanistic Insights to Targeting Strategies.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant immune cells in the lung cancer tumor microenvironment (TME), where their functions vary according to developmental origin, local signals, metabolic conditions, spatial location, and treatment exposure. However, clinical studies have not yet established the efficacy, selectivity, or safety of these approaches. Major challenges remain, including the high heterogeneity of TAMs, activation of compensatory pathways, systemic toxicity, and the translational gap between preclinical and clinical studies. Future research should focus on validating markers that distinguish disease-associated macrophage states from macrophages required for pulmonary homeostasis and integrating longitudinal tissue, circulating, spatial, and imaging biomarkers. Controlled clinical studies are required to determine whether macrophage-directed interventions can improve existing lung cancer treatments.

papers.title: Preserving malignant provenance in single-cell cancer atlases: lessons from Ewing sarcoma plasticity.
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases increasingly organize tumors according to recurrent transcriptional states, but state-based integration can weaken or obscure the molecular evidence that distinguishes malignant from non-malignant provenance. Although Ewing sarcoma provides the principal exemplar, the framework is designed for testing in other tumors in which plastic malignant states converge transcriptionally with non-malignant compartments.

Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear.ObjectiveTo define the cell type-specific effects of dupilumab in eCRS, we examined IL-4/IL-13 receptor-dependent transcriptional responses in tissue-resident immune cells.MethodsNasal polyp and peripheral blood samples were collected from five patients with eCRS before and after dupilumab treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing on four paired cases, spatial transcriptomics, and immunostaining were performed. In vitro stimulation of human conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) validated IL-4/IL-13-regulated pathways.ResultsDupilumab improved symptoms and attenuated eosinophilic inflammation. Across annotated populations, the number of differentially expressed genes correlated positively with pre-treatment IL13RA1 expression. Accordingly, myeloid cells, particularly cDCs, which predominantly express type II IL-4/IL-13 receptors, showed the broadest transcriptional changes, including downregulation of ALOX15; ALOX15 inhibition abrogated IL-4/IL-13-induced CCL13 and CCL22 expression in cDCs. After treatment, pathogenic Th2 cell subset expressed lower IL1RL1 and AREG. IGHE and IL4R expression in CD23-positive B cells declined, as did PRDM1 and ELL2 in plasma cells. In one paired case, spatial analysis identified fewer TLS-like aggregates and lower detection of ALOX15 and IGHE transcripts after treatment.ConclusionDupilumab preferentially remodels type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells, particularly polyp cDCs, while selectively reprogramming Th2, B, and plasma cells. Identification of ALOX15 as a candidate mediator in cDCs provides mechanistic insight that may inform optimization of type 2-targeted therapy in eCRS.

papers.title: BGN marks cancer-associated fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix remodeling in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Biglycan (BGN) is an important component of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Using an integrated analysis of TCGA bulk RNA-sequencing, single-cell RNA-sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic datasets, we systematically characterized the expression patterns, prognostic significance, and biological roles of BGN in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and survival analyses in independent clinical cohorts further validated the expression pattern, abundance, and prognostic significance of BGN. The biological role of BGN was further investigated using in vitro tumor cell-cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) co-culture systems, BGN knockdown, and subsequent phenotypic assays. Here, BGN was significantly upregulated in HNSCC tissues, and elevated BGN expression was associated with poorer patient prognosis. Higher BGN expression was also associated with increased mesenchymal scores, enrichment of pathways related to CAF activation, ECM remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), as well as potentially reduced sensitivity to commonly used chemotherapeutic agents. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that BGN was predominantly expressed by CAFs, with BGN-positive (BGN+) CAFs exhibiting markedly enhanced ECM remodeling activity and greater potential for intercellular communication. Spatial transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that BGN-high spots were preferentially localized within the stromal matrix and distant from the tumor core. Functionally, tumor cells co-cultured with BGN-knockdown CAFs exhibited reduced proliferation, colony-forming capacity, invasion, and migration, accompanied by suppression of the EMT phenotype. Collectively, these findings suggest that BGN may serve as a biomarker of an ECM/stromal remodeling-dominant CAF state in HNSCC and represent a potential therapeutic target for HNSCC.

papers.title: Cholesterol transporters and immune-metabolic features in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma receiving immunotherapy combinations.
papers.abstract: BackgroundDespite improved outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) combinations in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), reliable biologically-driven prognostic markers remain needed. The CHOMET study evaluated tumor ABCA1/ABCG1 expression and their association with systemic lipid parameters, nutritional status, nephrectomy status, and survival outcomes.MethodsCHOMET was a retrospective observational biomarker study including mRCC patients undergoing first-line ICI combinations. Tumor ABCA1 and ABCG1 expressions were assessed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), and the Controlling Nutritional Status score (CONUT) were collected. Publicly available transcriptomic datasets were used for exploratory bulk RNA-seq, immune deconvolution, and single-cell analyses.ResultsAmong 86 patients (46 with IHC), high ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression was associated with shorter overall survival (OS, P = .003 and P = .01) and progression-free survival (PFS, P = .05 and P = .08). A composite nephrectomy-cholesterol score and a lower CONUT score were both significantly associated with improved PFS and OS. Exploratory bulk RNA-seq analyses suggested that high ABCA1 expression correlated with features of an immunosuppressive microenvironment enriched in M2 macrophages and depleted of CD8+ T cells, whereas high ABCG1 expression correlated with increased regulatory T cells. Exploratory single-cell analyses from 4 patients showed ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression across tumor-associated macrophages and tumor cells, with donor-specific pathway enrichment patterns involving immune signaling and cholesterol metabolism-related transcriptional programs.ConclusionsABCA1 and ABCG1 expression levels were associated with poorer outcomes in mRCC treated with ICI combinations and support a link between cholesterol transport programs and an immunosuppressive, metabolically reprogrammed tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: The last gift cohort: advancing HIV reservoir research through single-cell and spatial approaches.
papers.abstract: Purpose of reviewDespite effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), persistent HIV reservoirs remain the primary obstacle to achieving an HIV cure. Understanding persistence requires defining not only reservoir size but also the identity and state of infected cells and their anatomical microenvironments - features that blood-based bulk measurements cannot resolve. We synthesize published findings from the Last Gift end-of-life cohort, in which longitudinal sampling and tissue donation via rapid autopsy have advanced our understanding of HIV persistence across anatomical compartments. We then highlight how integrated single-cell and spatial profiling can link proviral features to host-cell states and local tissue neighborhoods, helping to define the cellular and microenvironmental niches that sustain persistence.Recent findingsThe Last Gift studies have mapped HIV DNA and envelope diversity across up to 33 anatomical compartments, inferred lymphoid and gastrointestinal tissues to be dominant sources of viral dispersal, shown that >85% of expanded proviral clones are shared across tissues, and recovered inducible, replication-competent virus from parietal-cortex microglia. Single-cell profiling has resolved heterogeneous microglial transcriptional and chromatin states containing rare HIV RNA or accessible proviral DNA and has identified a transcriptomic definition of cells expressing HIV RNA despite viral suppression on ART. Additionally, mass cytometry of viral sensors and restriction factors has defined tissue- and cell subset-specific antiviral programs, including restriction-factor profiles in lymph-node follicular helper T-cells predicted to favor HIV persistence. In parallel, imaging-based spatial transcriptomics with custom HIV probes, immunoPET/CT-guided tissue sampling, and duplex RNAscope/DNAscope have made direct localization of viral nucleic acids within annotated tissue neighborhoods technically feasible. No single assay, however, establishes proviral intactness, transcriptional activity, cellular identity, spatial position, and neighborhoods at once.SummaryReservoir measurements should be reported by what each assay can establish rather than as interchangeable estimates of reservoir size. Cohorts such as the Last Gift, which yield matched blood and multiorgan tissue from the same donor with longitudinal clinical context, are well suited to applying direct proviral characterization, single-cell phenotyping and spatially resolved viral detection in parallel on the same specimens. This combination defines the resolution - intact provirus, in an identified cell, in a defined tissue niche - that cure trials should increasingly be expected to measure.

papers.title: Clinical success, mechanical stability, and Peri-implant radiographic characteristics of orthodontic mini-screws under immediate versus delayed loading: a retrospective comparative study.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare clinical success, mechanical stability, and peri‑implant radiographic characteristics of orthodontic mini-screws subjected to immediate loading (IL) versus delayed loading (DL).MethodsThis retrospective comparative study evaluated the clinical records of 100 orthodontic patients who received one orthodontic mini-screw in the maxilla or mandible. Implant stability was assessed using the Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) and Periotest values (PTV) at baseline and at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Peri-implant radiographic measurements were obtained using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) at the documented assessment time points. Failures included screw loss, mobility > grade 1, persistent inflammation > 2 weeks, or pain requiring removal. Survival was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier curves.ResultsClinical success was recorded in 47 of 50 mini-screws (94.0%) in the IL group and 46 of 50 (92.0%) in the DL group, with 3 and 4 documented failures, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess time to clinical failure. ISQ values showed a transient decrease at 1 month in both groups, followed by progressive recovery and stabilization by 6 months. PTV values changed inversely to ISQ, showing a corresponding temporary increase at 1 month and subsequent improvement thereafter. CBCT-measured peri‑implant bone density increased progressively at 6, 12, and 24 months compared with baseline in both groups. Insertion torque and removal torque values were similar between the two loading protocols.ConclusionsImmediate and delayed loading of orthodontic mini-screws were associated with similar observed clinical success proportions and mechanical stability measurements, with no clear between-group differences in the available peri‑implant radiographic findings. These results do not establish equivalence between loading protocols or directly demonstrate histological osseointegration.

papers.title: Robust optical metasurface heterostructures for prevention and treatment of peri-implantitis.
papers.abstract: Peri-implantitis poses significant challenges in the field of oral implantology, while the inherent antibacterial properties of implant abutments and their tight sealing with surrounding soft tissues play a vital role in the prevent and treatment of peri-implantitis. Herein, a robust optical metasurface CeOx/TiO2 heterostructure with gradient-distributed nanocavity structure was prepared on titanium surface by innovatively integrating plasma immersion ion implantation and thermal treatment technologies. The CeOx/TiO2 heterostructure with an optimized bandgap enhances light absorption in the second near-infrared region and a robust optical metasurface with gradient-distributed nanocavities improves the retention of NIR light by the light trap effect and increases the heat preservation capacity, leading to superior photothermal antibacterial activity in vitro and in vivo. Besides, with the existence of ceria, metasurface CeOx/TiO2 heterostructure shows antioxidant properties and can alleviate the local inflammatory microenvironment, promoting soft tissue sealing in vitro and in vivo by sequentially activating the "Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, Rap1 signaling pathway, and ECM-receptor interaction" cascade network. This study paves the way for developing novel dental implant abutments with antibacterial activities and soft tissue sealing properties based on optical metasurface heterostructures for prevention and treatment of peri-implantitis.

papers.title: IER3-N-cadherin axis contributes to apoptosis resistance in dermal fibroblasts under profibrotic conditions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Persistent activation and resistance to apoptosis of dermal fibroblasts contribute to pathological skin fibrosis. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in cell survival, but its role in cutaneous fibrosis remains unclear. We investigated the functional significance of IER3 in dermal fibroblasts and its potential contribution to fibrosis. Methods IER3 expression was examined in skin samples from patients with systemic sclerosis, keloids, and hypertrophic scars. Primary human dermal fibroblasts were stimulated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1). RNA sequencing, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, quantitative PCR, and flow cytometric apoptosis assays were performed to investigate the downstream mechanisms and functional consequences of IER3 expression. Results IER3 expression was increased in dermal fibroblasts within fibrotic skin lesions and was induced by TGF-β1 independently of SMAD3 and MEK/ERK signaling. Transcriptomic analysis identified CDH2 , encoding N-cadherin, as a downstream target of IER3. Moreover, TGF-β1 induced CDH2 expression in a SMAD3 phosphorylation-dependent manner. IER3 knockdown attenuated TGF-β1-induced CDH2 expression, whereas CDH2 knockdown did not affect IER3 expression. Furthermore, CDH2 knockdown enhanced staurosporine-induced apoptosis in TGF-β1-stimulated fibroblasts, accompanied by a shift in apoptosis-related gene expression toward a pro-apoptotic profile. Conclusion Our findings identify a previously unrecognized IER3-N-cadherin regulatory axis that may promote dermal fibroblast survival by suppressing apoptosis under profibrotic conditions. Targeting this pathway may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for persistent skin fibrosis.

papers.title: Cell state programs offer a potential axis for classifying neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) arise from hormone-producing cells in the gut and pancreas. Despite increasing incidence of these tumors, therapeutic options remain limited. Well-differentiated GEP-NETs are classified by anatomic site, morphology, and proliferation indices, but this approach offers limited prognostic resolution among phenotypically similar tumors and constrains personalization of treatment decisions. In this issue of the JCI, Karam, Hoffman, and colleagues profiled 38 pancreatic and small-intestinal NETs using joint single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing and projected the resulting malignant cell-associated programs onto matched spatial transcriptomes. Two conserved malignant states emerged: neuronal-like and secretory neuroendocrine. These states span a continuum in both organ sites, are enriched for largely different transcription factor motifs, and occupy distinct microenvironmental niches. Secretory program scores trended higher in metastatic disease and may carry prognostic value. Taken together, these data describe NET heterogeneity as a cell state axis linked to tissue architecture.

papers.title: SpaceBlocks: an expert-supervised workflow for cohort-level spatial transcriptomics analysis
papers.abstract: Summary Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has become a central tool in tissue biology, with multiple technologies addressing the issue from a different angle. Each platform imposes its own raw data format conventions, and few workflows address reproducible, scalable, cohort-level analyses while integrating expert-supervised decisions to strengthen computational and biological provenance. In this work, we present SpaceBlocks, a Snakemake workflow for reproducible cohort-level analysis of single-cell resolution-ST data that prioritizes expert supervision over full automation. SpaceBlocks homogenizes heterogeneous platform outputs into a common data format, whose structure is validated to ensure downstream processing. Comprehensive expert supervision is facilitated through per sample quality control and cell type annotation diagnostic visualizations, after which downstream analyses automatically follow. SpaceBlocks also allows the ingestion of technology-agnostic externally formatted data and provides interoperability with existing tools and technologies. We demonstrate the use of SpaceBlocks through the reanalysis of 37 samples from public Visium HD, Xenium 5K and MERSCOPE datasets. SpaceBlocks exhibited processing scalability across the three platforms. This reanalysis identified previously missed cell types in Visium HD and heterogeneous marker gene expression in MERSCOPE, highlighting the need for expert-supervised annotations. Moreover, SpaceBlocks facilitated the identification of differentially expressed genes associated with previously defined multiple sclerosis (MS) spatial domains in MERSCOPE, and transcriptional differences between healthy and malignant colorectal tissues in Visium HD. Together, these findings establish SpaceBlocks as a flexible and reproducible workflow for expert-supervised spatial transcriptomics analysis across technologies and biological cohorts. Availability and Implementation SpaceBlocks is freely available under the MIT license on GitHub https://github.com/cbib/SpaceBlocks and the official Snakemake catalog https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-workflow-catalog/docs/workflows/cbib/SpaceBlocks.html . SpaceBlocks v0.5.1 code, config files, and the public data formatting scripts used to reproduce the results from this study have been deposited in Zenodo (doi: 10.5281/zenodo.23378236). Contact macha.nikolski@u-bordeaux.fr ; sergiooterino@usal.es Supplementary information Supplementary information is available online. Conflict of interest: None declared.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics decoding of the host response to Klebsiella pneumoniae infection reveals an itaconate-centred metabolic-immune axis and a spatially organised inflammatory programme
papers.abstract: Background Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) is a leading cause of hospital and community acquired pneumonia and bacteraemia, and hypervirulent and carbapenem resistant lineages continue to expand worldwide. Although individual omics layers of Kp infection have been profiled, the host-level molecular logic that connects transcriptional, cellular, metabolic and spatial programmes has not been systematically integrated. Methods We curated 16 public datasets spanning four modalities-bulk and dual host pathogen RNA-seq (six datasets; 118 libraries), single-cell RNA-seq (four datasets; ≈164,000 cells), untargeted/targeted metabolomics (four datasets; 1,842 molecular features) and Visium spatial transcriptomics (two datasets; ≈11,400 spots) covering murine lung infection models, hypervirulent and classical Kp strains, carbapenem-resistant isolates and human clinical specimens. Datasets were harmonised through a standardised pipeline (Salmon/DESeq2; Scanpy/Harmony; MetaboAnalyst; RCTD/spacexr), and integrated by WGCNA, GSVA, CellChat, Monocle3, SCENIC, joint-pathway analysis, RCTD deconvolution, and machine-learning feature selection (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with 1,000x bootstrap internal validation and independent external validation. Results Kp infection evoked a coherent 920 gene neutrophil inflammatory response (≈520 up-/≈400 down-regulated genes) dominated by IL-17/TNF/NF-κB signalling, neutrophil degranulation, HIF-1α-linked glycolysis and itaconate biosynthesis. A turquoise co-expression module (r = 0.86 with infection status) yielded a ten-gene hub signature (IRG1, S100A9, IL1B, CXCL2, SLC7A11, HMOX1, PTGS2, NFKBIA, LST1, FCGR3B). Single-cell profiling resolved twelve major lung lineages and eleven myeloid substates, tracing a Monocle3 trajectory from Cxcr2 hi inflammatory neutrophils through an Irg1/Slc7a11 hi oxidative phase into Cxcr4 hi /Trem2 hi suppressive states; CellChat identified S100A8/A9-TLR4 and CXCL2-CXCR2 as the most amplified axes (8.5x and 4.2x). Metabolomics revealed 30-fold pulmonary itaconate accumulation together with succinate and lactate elevation, glucose/glutamine depletion and glutathione collapse, and joint-pathway analysis positioned the TCA-cycle itaconate and ferroptosis modules as the strongest convergent perturbations. Spatial transcriptomics mapped these programmes onto five anatomical niches, with IRG1 expression peaking in the infection core (58% neutrophil content) and declining radially. A ten-gene host-response classification model reached AUC=0.958 in discovery, 0.937 in internal validation and 0.884-0.912 in two independent external cohorts (Brier score 0.071). Conclusions By vertically integrating public multi-omics data, we define an itaconate-centred metabolic-immune axis that couples inflammatory myeloid expansion to spatially segregated metabolic niches, and we deliver a validated host-side molecular signature that discriminates Kp infection from non-infected states.

papers.title: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heritable cardiac disorder commonly linked to alterations in desmosomal proteins. While desmosomal dysfunction is a recognized pathogenic mechanism, the early molecular remodeling that precedes clinical manifestations remains unclear. Here we used a mouse model with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific knockout of Pkp2 (encoding plakophilin-2) and performed time-resolved mass spectrometry-based proteomics to map disease progression from early PKP2 loss to structural remodeling. Molecular changes preceded phenotypic abnormalities, and spatial asymmetry was evident, with earlier and more pronounced proteome remodeling in the right ventricle despite comparable PKP2 depletion in both ventricles. Downregulation of protein networks spanning desmosomes, sarcomeres and mitochondria suggests their functional coupling, with mitochondrial remodeling emerging as an early and progressively worsening feature. Intervention with honokiol attenuated changes across the major protein networks, highlighting mitochondrial pathways as promising therapeutic targets and honokiol as a potential strategy to delay arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy progression. Our findings provide critical insights into the concealed stage of disease progression and identify molecular targets for early intervention.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte Identity Crisis Without Regenerative Re-entry: A Multi-Scale Atlas of Incomplete Dedifferentiation and Intercellular Communication Rewiring in the Infarcted Human Heart
papers.abstract: Background Adult mammalian hearts regenerate poorly after myocardial infarction (MI) because cardiomyocytes largely, though not absolutely, exit the cell cycle during postnatal maturation, yet the molecular logic connecting maturation, disease-associated dedifferentiation, and intercellular communication remains unclear. papers.title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit. We combined publicly available human transcriptomic resources, genetics-driven causal inference, machine-learning-assisted biomarker screening, mouse-derived single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases, immune-cell deconvolution, and in-silico molecular docking. Twenty migraine-related genes were detected with causal associations to ischaemic-stroke risk. We prioritised three consensus hub genes: CD79A, PKN2, and PRKDC. In stroke patients, CD79A was significantly downregulated, while PKN2 and PRKDC exhibited elevated expression; their reliable diagnostic capacity was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling mapped these hub genes to endothelial, myeloid and glial cell populations residing within a dynamic inflammatory-vascular pathological niche in mouse ischaemic brain lesions. Mechanistic analyses pointed to perturbed mitochondrial energy homeostasis and dysregulated adaptive immune responses as downstream consequences modulated by these hub genes. Molecular-docking simulations demonstrated high-affinity interactions between Tamibarotene, Dirithromycin and the three encoded hub proteins, highlighting these compounds as promising candidates for drug repurposing. Collectively, our multi-omics analysis pinpoints CD79A, PKN2 and PRKDC as migraine-derived causal targets for ischaemic stroke, delivers cell- and spatial-resolved mechanistic perspectives on neurovascular-unit injury, and puts forward lead compounds awaiting further pre-clinical validation.

papers.title: Stromal APOL4 defines a cancer-associated fibroblast state that organizes a chemosensitive niche in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Despite initial high response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, most patients eventually develop resistance, and the contribution of the tumor microenvironment to treatment outcomes has remained underexplored relative to tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms. APOL4 specifically marked a transcriptionally distinct CAF subtype (CAF-1) that extended beyond canonical CAF states and exhibited high matrix metalloproteinase and immune-activating cytokine expression. APOL4 knockdown attenuated the CAF-1 transcriptional program, and in 3D tumor-CAF co-cultures conferred carboplatin resistance to 12 of 14 ovarian cancer cell lines, providing causal evidence that stromal APOL4 supports platinum sensitivity in a tumor cell-extrinsic manner. NicheNet analysis revealed bidirectionally asymmetric communication: CAF-1 engaged non-stressed cancer cells through epithelial integrity-supporting axes, whereas other CAFs preferentially reinforced stressed, drug-tolerant cancer cells through canonical chemoresistance circuits. High-resolution Xenium spatial transcriptomics revealed a contact-restricted spatial association between CAF-1 proximity and reduced cancer-cell stress, defining a low-stress, immune-infiltrated niche that is spatially and compositionally distinct from the stress-enriched, immune-poor niche associated with CAF-2, with CAF-3 sharing features of both compartments. These findings identify stromal APOL4-CAF-1 as a prognostic biomarker and a functional contributor linking stromal matrix remodeling to platinum sensitivity and associated with an immune-infiltrated microenvironment, highlighting CAF-1-targeted strategies to enhance chemotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Autoimmune-shared immune states converge in a CXCL12-CXCR4 fibroblast-immune niche in chronic antibody-mediated rejection.
papers.abstract: Chronic antibody-mediated rejection (CAMR) is a leading cause of late kidney allograft failure and shares features of chronic immune activation with systemic autoimmune diseases, but how circulating immune states connect to spatially organized graft injury and whether related immune features recur in autoimmune inflammation remain unclear. These subsets showed migratory and tissue-interacting transcriptional features, including recurrent CXCR4 and ZEB2 expression, suggesting candidate immune states potentially linked to local graft immune organization. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics localized this fibroblast-immune architecture to perivascular regions marked by endothelial activation and stromal remodeling and placed CAMR-associated immune states within adjacent immune-rich neighborhoods, supporting a CXCL12-CXCR4 axis that may be associated with local immune accumulation. Comparisons with large-scale blood immune reference data and spatial transcriptomic datasets from rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus suggested partial recurrence of related immune states and fibroblast-immune organization. Together, this study links circulating CAMR immune remodeling to a spatially organized CXCL12-CXCR4 fibroblast-immune niche and suggests that elements of this niche recur across alloimmune and autoimmune inflammation.

papers.title: Multiomics Dissection of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer (EOCRC) Reveals an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment and Identifies FAT3 Mutation as a Biomarker of Hot-Like Immune Features.
papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) exhibits distinct clinical and biological features compared with late-onset CRC (LOCRC), yet its genomic architecture and immune microenvironmental determinants remain incompletely characterized. Mutational signature decomposition showed that EOCRC was associated with an SBS87-like signature, whereas LOCRC was dominated by SBS1; because TCGA lacks detailed treatment history, this SBS87-like inference should not be interpreted as direct evidence of prior thiopurine exposure. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis identified a mitochondrial-ribosomal biogenesis module as the transcriptional hallmark of EOCRC. Integrative single-cell analysis localized FAT3 predominantly to cancer-associated fibroblasts, especially myofibroblasts, and an in silico FAT3 perturbation analysis suggested potential downstream programs involving extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory signaling, chemokine response, and mitotic spindle regulation. These findings delineate age-stratified genomic and microenvironmental features of EOCRC and generate testable hypotheses for future functional and clinical validation.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics identifies tumor-intrinsic and stromal programs associated with immune exclusion in NSCLC.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has reshaped the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains limited to a subset of patients. One major pattern of resistance is immune exclusion, in which CD8+ T cells accumulate in stromal regions but fail to penetrate tumor nests. Here, using discovery and non-overlapping internal validation cohorts of ICB-treated NSCLC patients, we show that spatial CD8+ T-cell exclusion is associated with lower objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival. papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts: origins, functional heterogeneity and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are integral components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of nearly every hallmark of cancer. Once viewed as a uniform, protumorigenic cell type, it is now clear that CAFs comprise a spectrum of dynamic and plastic functional states with both tumor-promoting and tumor-restraining capacities. This functional duality, conceptualized within the framework of cancer as a "wound that fails to heal", is dictated by their diverse cellular origins, the specific activation pathways engaged (such as TGF-β and PDGF), and the evolving cues from the TME. In this Review, we dissect the multifaceted roles of CAFs, from their promotion of cancer cell proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis through secreted factors and extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, to their profound influence on the immune landscape. We detail how distinct CAF subsets, such as myofibroblastic (myCAFs) and inflammatory (iCAFs) CAFs, orchestrate an immunosuppressive niche and contribute to therapeutic resistance. We also explore the compelling evidence for tumor-suppressive CAF functions, which have catalyzed a paradigm shift in therapeutic strategies-moving away from indiscriminate CAF ablation towards nuanced approaches aimed at reprogramming their state. These strategies include modulating key signaling pathways, normalizing the CAF-remodeled ECM, and exploiting unique metabolic vulnerabilities. Finally, we discuss how advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are resolving this complexity, paving the way for the development of precision therapies that can selectively neutralize pro-tumorigenic CAF activities while harnessing their beneficial functions to improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal cancer characterized by a high abundance of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which influence therapy response, tumor biology and tumor aggressiveness. No associations were observed between mutational signatures and the abundance of CAF and epithelial tumor subtypes. Interestingly, a high abundance of CAFs, and specifically increased iCAF abundance, was associated with improved survival. papers.title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: AimsCarotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. papers.title: Sialylation-Siglec glyco-immune checkpoints in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of immune evasion, therapeutic resistance, and postoperative recurrence.
papers.abstract: Postoperative recurrence and incomplete responses to immunotherapy remain major obstacles to the long-term control of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Tumor-associated sialylation may promote immune escape by generating glycans that bind inhibitory members of the sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectin (Siglec) family on immune cells. This review critically examines HCC-specific evidence on abnormal sialylation, Siglec-related dysfunction of natural killer cells and macrophages, treatment-associated glycan remodeling, and possible links to molecular residual disease and postoperative recurrence. Glycan patterns vary substantially between tumors and within individual tumors. Total sialic acid abundance and the expression of a single sialyltransferase therefore provide only part of the information needed to identify functional Siglec ligands. Their activity also depends on glycan structure, chemical modifications, the molecule carrying the glycan, ligand density, surface accessibility, and spatial organization. The strongest HCC-specific evidence concerns the interaction between Siglec-9 and natural killer cells. Supporting findings include receptor and ligand expression, close spatial proximity within tumors, associations with adverse clinical outcomes, and recovery of natural killer-cell activity after pathway inhibition in preclinical models. Siglec-10-high tumor-associated macrophages are associated with an immunosuppressive myeloid state. Their endogenous ligands and receptor-specific roles in vivo require further characterization. In sorafenib-resistant HCC models, increased ST3 β-galactoside α-2,3-sialyltransferase 1 (ST3GAL1) expression accompanies greater Siglec-7 and Siglec-9 probe binding, while ST3GAL1 silencing improves natural killer-cell-mediated cytotoxicity. These findings support a functional contribution of altered glycosylation to treatment-related immune escape. Glycocalyx-dependent changes in adhesion, migration, and survival may also contribute to dissemination and residual-cell persistence alongside immune evasion. Direct studies are now needed to determine whether sialylation-Siglec signaling helps residual HCC cells survive after curative-intent therapy. Clinical translation will require identification of specific glycan-carrier pairs, spatial mapping of receptor-ligand contacts, receptor-specific validation in species-appropriate models, and prospective evaluation of glyco-immune biomarkers alongside circulating tumor DNA and established clinicopathological factors across HCC etiologies. Overall, current evidence identifies the sialylation-Siglec system as a biologically plausible and cell-specific immune-evasion network. It also provides a framework for biomarker-guided evaluation of Siglec-directed therapies and tumor-targeted desialylation and future studies of its contribution to HCC recurrence.

papers.title: Evaluating the Ethical and Clinical Reliability of Large Language Models in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a subject of great interest as a clinical decision-support tool, but their reliability is not well described in the surgical field of oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS). The responses were evaluated independently by two OMFS board-certified surgeons on an ordinal scale of 0–2 in three areas: clinical accuracy, ethical safety, and risk awareness. Mean scores were calculated and non-parametric comparisons were made. Results All models demonstrated high clinical accuracy (mean ± SD: GPT-4: 1.85 ± 0.42; Claude 3: 1.90 ± 0.38; Gemini: 1.75 ± 0.48), but exhibited significant variability in ethical safety (Claude 3: 1.75 ± 0.45; GPT-4: 1.60 ± 0.58; Gemini: 1.50 ± 0.52; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.004). The post hoc tests showed that the ethical safety scores differed significantly between Claude 3 and Gemini (Dunn's test, p = 0.008). A human in the loop structure and the ethics tuning pertaining to the domain are necessary prior to clinical integration. These tools should be used as a complementary support tool in a well-defined framework of human-in-the-loop, until domain-specific ethical tuning and real-world validation are attained. Thus, clinical decision-making and patient safety are well protected under the authority of a qualified surgeon.

papers.title: The tumor suppressor role of the KRAS proto-oncogene in metastatic pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS is the most frequently mutated proto-oncogene in human cancers. Progression to advanced disease is frequently associated with allelic imbalance of the KRAS locus with gain of the mutant allele and loss of the wild-type allele through clonal and sub-clonal loss of heterozygosity (LOH). Cross species analysis leveraging research autopsies and surgical specimens revealed that KRAS-LOH is associated with metastatic dissemination and shorter overall survival. Transcriptomic analysis through single-cell RNA sequencing uncovered a conserved phenomenon whereby KRAS-LOH is paralleled by an immune evasive phenotype through loss of the tumor-cell interferon response and reduced CD8+ T cell infiltration. In line with this evidence, orthotopic transplants of isogenic tumor populations differing for the Kras allelic status demonstrated that only cancer cells with Kras-LOH are are able to form tumors in immune competent animals. papers.title: MetaEntropy: quantifying protein variability in complex viral mixtures via entropy
papers.abstract: High-density sequence data has become commonplace in the study of complex viral mixtures from wastewater. Established algorithms are available for lineage deconvolution and labelling of clinically-elusive mutations. MetaEntropy integrates utility functions for visualizing genome-wide and protein-specific variability, extracting nucleotide and amino acid mutation profiles, and identifying entropy hotspots. Despite being designed for wastewater surveillance, the package can also profile protein diversity from cross-sectional intra-patient data. However, it does not analyze population structure or quasispecies, for which several tools are available. By focusing on positional entropy, MetaEntropy bypasses the sequence constraints, computational overhead, and consensus-based variant loss typical of traditional haplotype reconstruction and multiple sequence alignment strategies. To balance sensitivity against neutral variation, the package evaluates entropy using a standard 20-class canonical amino acid scheme and a 7-class model based on traditional physicochemical properties. Calculated entropy values are normalized to a 0-1 scale, enabling direct comparisons of protein diversity across loci and sample strata. As proofs of concept, we employ MetaEntropy to detect well-known SARS-CoV-2 functional changes from wastewater data, and to explore tissue-specific heterogeneity in systemic infections. papers.title: Distinct spatial domains of auxin perception control root growth in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Primary root morphogenesis is coordinated by the integrated action of cell division, expansion, and differentiation. papers.title: All the diversity we cannot see: Using single-cell population genetics to reveal the reproductive mode of the snow alga Chlainomonas sp. (Chlorophyta)
papers.abstract: Many organisms responsible for globally important processes, from carbon cycling to human disease, are microscopic eukaryotes. While their reproduction is essential for their success, across the tree of life, our understanding of evolutionary processes is limited due to the inherent challenges of studying microorganisms. Tools and predictions developed in multicellular and obligately sexual taxa are often not tractable in microbes, where population sizes can be large and extracting DNA from individuals is difficult. Even when sexual characteristics can be observed, population genetics is the only method available to characterize the reproductive mode. The relative rates of sexual versus clonal reproduction partition genetic diversity and are therefore integral to our understanding of evolutionary processes. This Chlorophyte alga exhibits a complex life cycle, whereby bloom dynamics are directly observable in natural populations. We explored genetic diversity using single cells collected across several years of Chlainomonas sp. summer blooms. Dominant red cells in the bloom were diploid. Yet, all were unique genotypes, despite the prediction that clonal processes drive bloom development. We found high selfing rates, but selfing and clonality are often indistinguishable without understanding an organisms's natural history. Chlainomonas sp. has a haploid-diploid life cycle as hypothesized, engaging in both clonal and sexual reproduction, likely selfing. This study represents a first use of single cell population genetic methods to understand natural populations of partially clonal microeukaryotes.

papers.title: scPACE: A Personalized Autoencoder for Cell Evolution in Single-Cell Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Single-cell studies increasingly profile large cohorts of individuals, measuring thousands of cells in each donor. papers.title: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. papers.title: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell
papers.abstract: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. papers.title: Continuous karyotypic and cryptic structural fluctuations drive acral melanoma evolution
papers.abstract: Reliable chromosome segregation during mitosis is essential for high-fidelity mammalian cell division. Even human cancers burdened by whole genome duplication and aneuploidy generally retain sufficiently stable segregation to produce clonal populations of progeny. Cancer genomes are accordingly understood to evolve in punctuated bursts, in which catastrophic rearrangement is followed by clonal expansion of a stabilized karyotype. However, bulk genomic sequencing, the workhorse of cancer genetics for the past two decades, cannot resolve structural variability within tumor subpopulations. Here we identify a subset of cancers that exhibit continuous ultra-low fidelity chromosomal segregation, with single tumors harboring individual cells whose metaphase chromosome counts ranged from 25 to over 200. This remarkable phenotype is recurrent in multiple cancer types and most common in acral melanoma, where it is associated with dicentric chromosomes, translocations, and complex structural variants. Single-cell whole genome sequencing revealed ongoing structural variation and the genomic signature of microhomology-mediated break-induced replication (MMBIR), a backup DNA repair pathway that triggers chromoanasynthesis. These genomes therefore do not pass through isolated catastrophic events and settle into stable lineages but rather undergo continuous evolution of chromosome number and structure across generations, resulting in extreme intratumoral heterogeneity and a shifting repertoire of gene fusions. We anticipate these findings will serve as a starting point for classifying tumors by ongoing karyotypic and structural fluctuation and for testing whether this state confers selective dependence on backup repair pathways.

papers.title: A cytoskeletal toggle switch controls amnion architecture and fate
papers.abstract: Binary cellular decisions are generally attributed to gene regulatory networks, with cytoskeletal-driven shape changes often treated as an output. Yet, whether the cytoskeleton can itself implement switch-like logic to drive abrupt morphological transitions remains unknown. In the primate amniotic sac, the extraembryonic amnion derives directly from the columnar epiblast and abruptly flattens into a squamous epithelium to form a highly asymmetric cavity. Here, we identify a cytoskeletal switch driving this developmental bifurcation in human gastrula models. Mutual inhibition between actomyosin and keratin networks generates two mechanical attractors: amnion cells flip into a keratin-rich, squamous shape, while the epiblast remains myosin-rich and columnar. Ectopic activation of YAP1-TEAD signaling triggers the myosin-keratin switch without inducing amnion specification, establishing that the switch is not simply a consequence of fate changes. Conversely, preventing the switch disrupts amnion specification, showing that this shape bifurcation gates lineage commitment. Single-cell transcriptomics across cytoskeletal perturbations revealed a transcriptional signature for the toggle switch, which is recapitulated in vivo in the human and marmoset amnion. Together, our findings show that the cytoskeleton acts not only as an effector of tissue shape but as a decision-making module, implementing the same toggle switch logic as gene regulatory networks to drive morphological bifurcations.

papers.title: Minute-scale single-cell transcriptomics reveals a temporal grammar of inflammatory responses
papers.abstract: Inflammatory stimulation triggers transient pulses, sustained activation, and repression, yet the principles organizing these distinct transcriptional kinetics remain unclear. papers.abstract: The extension of human lifespan is accompanied by a growing burden of chronic disease and multimorbidity. papers.title: Biased evolution of pollen size after whole genome duplication
papers.abstract: Cell size is an important functional attribute of single-celled organisms, and whole genome duplication (WGD) has long been hypothesized to double the volume of unicells.
