Finally, in 16 autotetraploid-diploid pairs, the differences in pollen size were not correlated with the differences in their 1Cx DNA content. Community functional potential remained largely stable throughout the experiment, although phosphorus accumulation failed during phases of high mass transfer. Repeated connectivity promoted compositional similarity beyond periods of active dispersal while maintaining invasion resistance and functional stability, highlighting controlled dispersal as a promising community-level strategy for managing complex microbial communities.

papers.title: Delivered but Discharged Without Assessment: A National Multilevel Analysis of Missed Maternal Postpartum Assessment Before Discharge After Facility Birth in Ethiopia, 2024/2025 EDHS
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Missed maternal postnatal assessment before discharge after facility birth is an undermeasured indicator of intrafacility quality of care that previous Ethiopian studies did not isolate in nationally representative analyses. papers.title: LIFE-seq: longitudinal spatial transcriptomics of living tissue
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has deepened our understanding of cellular spatial heterogeneity, yet existing technologies are predominantly confined to fixed or frozen specimens, limiting longitudinal molecular profiling of the same living tissue. By enabling repeated molecular sampling and spatial transcriptomic analysis of living tissue, LIFE-seq provides a versatile framework for investigating tissue dynamics and pathological progression in vivo .

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Age-Specific Cancer Hallmark Architecture in Pediatric and Adult Brain Tumors
papers.abstract: Pediatric cancers are fundamentally different from their adult counterparts. Specifically, pediatric cancers carry fewer mutations, interact with developing immune systems, and have active developmental microenvironments. The tumor microenvironment (TME), which includes the surrounding stromal cells, immune cells, blood vessels, and extracellular matrix, plays a crucial role in cancer progression, metastasis, behavior, and treatment response. To better understand the effects of the pediatric tumor microenvironment on tumor gene expression, we acquired spatial transcriptomic data from 17 pediatric brain tumor samples and analyzed it through a Cancer Hallmarks framework. Cancer Hallmarks, as outlined by Hanahan and Weinberg, provide a comprehensive set of 14 biological capabilities that cancers acquire to enable tumor growth and metastasis. We compared the spatial gene expression patterns of the Cancer Hallmarks gene sets between the TME and neoplastic compartments in pediatric brain tumors. Compared with a similar study of adult brain tumors, in which Cancer Hallmark expression patterns clearly separated the TME and neoplastic compartments, we identified three hallmarks (“Deregulating Cellular Energetics,” “Senescent Cells,” and “Evading Growth Suppressors”) whose predominant cellular compartments differed between pediatric and adult tumors. In pediatric samples, these hallmarks were associated primarily with the TME rather than the neoplastic compartment. This shift implicates an age-specific rewiring of the tumor ecosystem. We also provide clear evidence of strong transcriptomic regulation in genes shared by pediatric and adult neoplastic compartments. Finally, we show how measures of spatial autocorrelation may be used to distinguish tumor grade. Significance Distinguishing between pediatric and adult tumors is essential for tailoring treatments to specific age groups and discovering new interactions between the tumor microenvironment (TME) and neoplasms. Pediatric brain tumors exhibit distinct biological features compared to their adult counterparts, including lower mutational burden and unique immune responses. However, whether these differences manifest primarily in tumors, the TME, or both has been unclear. In this study, we systematically compare the Cancer Hallmarks architecture using existing spatial transcriptomic gene sets and ask whether each set is more frequently observed in the neoplastic compartment versus the TME of pediatric tumors. By preserving the spatial resolution of gene expression, our findings elucidate pediatric tumor pathways, genetic factors, and how these interact with surrounding tissue. This framework may clarify how age-associated developmental programs shape growth-promoting states in pediatric tumors and their TME.

papers.title: Visual Landmarks Influence Eye-Hand Coordination in Memory-Guided Reaches
papers.abstract: The human visual system optimally weighs egocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to the eye) and allocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to other landmarks) to aim actions. In the temporal domain, landmarks reduced gaze reaction time, increased the time to final hand touch, and reduced gaze-hand coupling. Landmark shifts increased errors in pooled datasets, due to weighted (and modestly correlated) shifts in both reach and gaze in the same direction. The 'allocentric weights' for reach were also modulated by initial gaze position. Overall, these data suggest that visual landmarks influence the timing, accuracy, and coordination of gaze / hand movements, likely through visual feedback during reach, and these effectors share a similar mechanism for optimal integration of egocentric and allocentric visual cues.

papers.title: Switches in single-neuron excitability class can induce rich dynamical states in balanced networks

papers.title: p53 supports healthy aging
papers.abstract: p53 is a master regulator of cellular stress responses that is also implicated in the aging process. papers.title: RUNX1-Mediated Hypoxic Signaling Impairs Myogenesis and Promotes Fibrosis in Myopathies.
papers.abstract: Compromised myogenic repair with enhanced fibrosis is common in myopathies, including Wooden Breast (WB) myopathy in broilers, but the underlying mechanism of their co-occurrence remains elusive. Using WB myopathy as a model, we investigated the common pathological origins of these co-occurring features. Our single-nucleus RNA sequencing results showed enhanced oxidative stress and profibrotic remodeling of myofibers, increased proliferation but decreased differentiation of satellite cells (SCs), and aggravated differentiation of fibroblasts (FBs) in WB samples. Differential gene expression and pseudotime trajectory analysis further identified RUNX1 as a key regulator for both SCs and FBs, which was further supported by gene functional studies in respective cell culture models. Moreover, reduced blood flow and oxygen supply may indicate a hypoxic state in WB muscle, which was associated with enhanced RUNX1 expression. Consistently, coordinately enhanced HIF1A and RUNX1 expressions were found in differentiated FBs of human muscles and in muscles with diseases. Collectively, our study found that hypoxia-associated upregulation of RUNX1 disrupted the myogenic progression of SCs and exacerbated fibrotic differentiation of FBs, contributing to pathological degeneration in myopathies. Targeting RUNX1 may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for prevention and treatment, which warrants future in vivo investigations.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomic Analysis Reveals an EBV-Associated MIF-SPP1+ Macrophage Axis Linking Tumor Stemness and Immune Dysfunction in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Elucidating how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) shapes tumor-immune interactions is important for improving therapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This multi-cohort analysis integrates single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data with multiplex immunofluorescence and functional assays. Single-cell profiling identifies stemness-associated epithelial states and enrichment of SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in EBV+ NPC. SPP1+ TAM abundance is associated with stemness-associated epithelial features and dysfunctional T-cell states, while high MIF and SPP1+ macrophage signatures are associated with shorter progression-free survival. Within the EBV+ spatial cohort, SPP1+ TAMs co-occur with stemness-associated tumor cells, exhausted CD8+ T cells, and regulatory T cells in Niche 5, which is more frequent in non-response tumors following chemoimmunotherapy. Functional experiments show increased MIF expression and secretion by EBV+ epithelial cells. MIF inhibition attenuates conditioned-medium-induced monocyte migration and SPP1-associated TAM-like programming, whereas recombinant MIF reproduces these effects. Conversely, macrophage-derived SPP1 increases stemness-associated marker expression and tumorsphere formation in EBV+ epithelial and tumor models. It also impairs primary CD8+ T-cell proliferation, effector function, and cytotoxic activity while increasing exhaustion-associated markers; CD44 blockade partially reverses these effects. Collectively, these findings support an EBV-associated MIF-SPP1 macrophage-tumor/T-cell crosstalk model linking stemness-associated epithelial phenotypes with immune dysfunction and adverse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Polymeric Biomaterials with Multiple Stratified Layers for Periodontal Ligament/Bone Regeneration: A Review.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic pathological condition initiated by bacterial plaque accumulation and characterized by the progressive destruction of the tooth-supporting tissues, including the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone. If left untreated, it may result in tooth mobility, pathologic tooth migration, and ultimately tooth loss. Despite numerous regenerative strategies, complete periodontal regeneration remains challenging. Guided tissue regeneration (GTR) and guided bone regeneration (GBR) promote the regeneration of the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone; however, current GTR/GBR biomaterials often exhibit inadequate mechanical stability and osseointegration. To overcome these limitations, various multilayer biomaterials with enhanced functionalities have been developed. This review outlines the key properties required for GTR/GBR, evaluates the design and performance of current multilayer biomaterials, and examines their major limitations, particularly their inability to fully replicate native periodontal tissues due to structural incompatibilities between layers. Finally, future directions and recommendations are presented to guide the development of next-generation GTR/GBR biomaterials.

papers.title: Rational Surface Engineering Reduces Advanced Glycation End-Product Adsorption and Improves Implant Integration.
papers.abstract: Advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) accumulate in metabolic diseases such as diabetes and are closely associated with poor outcomes following implantation. However, how these molecules influence events at the biomaterial interface has remained largely unknown. Here, we identify AGEs as critical biointerfacial modifiers that adsorb onto implant surfaces, reprogram immune responses, promote fibrotic encapsulation, impair angiogenesis, and compromise osseointegration. This suggests a potential mechanism by which metabolic disease disrupts biomaterial-tissue integration. By engineering titanium surfaces enriched with amine or carboxyl functionalities, we create AGE-resistant biointerfaces that effectively suppress pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization, promote an anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage phenotype, reduce fibrotic encapsulation, enhance angiogenesis, and improve osseointegration across ex vivo, in vitro, and in vivo diabetic models. These findings establish disease-informed surface chemistry as a design paradigm for next-generation implants intended for metabolically compromised and other high-risk patient populations.

papers.title: The association between vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1 signaling on dural macrophages and pain.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is expressed on various cells, including vascular endothelial cells, and has a variety of functions; VEGF receptor (VEGFR) is expressed not only on vascular endothelial cells but also on monocytes and macrophages. Although dural macrophages have been found to be abundant along dural blood vessels, their association with neurological diseases remains unclear. This present study focused on VEGFR1 and explored the role of dural macrophages in a mouse model of neuropathic pain. Intrathecal administration of VEGF-A and VEGF-B lowered the pain threshold, accumulated dural macrophages around blood vessels, and increased the expression of inflammatory cytokines. Administration of VEGFR inhibitors to fourth lumbar nerve-injured mice significantly increased the pain threshold. These findings suggest that VEGF/VEGFR signaling is associated with dural macrophage accumulation and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in the dura mater. These inflammatory responses may represent an additional mechanism associated with pain hypersensitivity.

papers.title: Evaluation of the accuracy of zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation using a fully digital workflow versus conventional protocol: a randomized clinical trial.
papers.abstract: The zygomatic bone has multiple points of articulation with the craniofacial skeleton, and accurate intraoperative reduction in various planes is very challenging and entirely dependent on the operator's subjective evaluation. This study aimed to investigate the efficiency of a novel fully digital protocol versus the conventional management strategy for zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation. Twenty-eight patients with acute zygomatic fractures who met the inclusion criteria were recruited; each group of 14 patients was randomly assigned. The intervention group received a fully digital protocol, represented by customized predictive-hole surgical guides and patient-specific fixation plates, while the control group was managed conventionally. Accuracy of bone reduction was the primary outcome. The results showed that, when comparing the virtual reduction of both groups with the postoperative CT scans, the overall accuracy was markedly higher in the digital group (0.290 ± 0.132 mm) than in the conventional group (1.290 ± 0.525 mm), with a mean difference of -1.000 mm (95% CI -1.309 to -0.691; p < 0.001) and a very large effect size (d = -2.612). Clinically, the digital group showed higher patient satisfaction with aesthetics and a shorter operation duration, while no difference in infraorbital nerve numbness was observed between the two groups. Based on the statistical and clinical findings of this study, a fully digital workflow provided a valuable approach for the management of zygomaticomaxillary complex fractures, optimizing aesthetic and functional rehabilitation.

papers.title: The late effects of head and neck cancer treatment - a scoping review.
papers.abstract: IntroductionThere has been a change in the clinical outcomes associated with head and neck cancers (HNC) over the past decade. More patients are living beyond 5 years, following their HNC treatment. Consequently, survivorship has become increasingly important, driving the need to research and treat the late effects of HNC therapies. The aim of this study was to map the range of late effects reported by patients in the literature.Materials and methodsWe undertook a scoping review of current literature to identify the late effects of head and neck cancer treatment reported, with the aim to create a potential list of items for a Patient Concerns Inventory for Head and Neck Cancer (PCI-H&N). Studies reporting on any late effect of head and neck cancer in human adults, existing at least five years after treatment, were included.ResultsAfter removal of duplicates, 298 records were screened; 270 were excluded (including one report that could not be retrieved), and 28 were included in our final review. The studies investigated chronic physical symptoms, as well as psychological and social impacts. Articles reported on a variety of different late effects, with little consistency between articles.ConclusionHead and neck cancer survivors experience a wide range of long-term symptoms and effects on their day-to-day activities. Qualitative evidence to guide the selection of the impacts that are important to people following HNC treatment is lacking. Further qualitative research would support a better understanding of the range and relative importance of late effects for individuals treated for head and neck cancer. This will enable clinicians to provide long-term, holistic multidisciplinary care for head and neck cancer survivors and hopefully improve their overall quality of life.

papers.title: The impact of socioeconomic status on congenital upper limb difference registry inclusion.
papers.abstract: Clinical registries are essential for advancing research in rare conditions such as congenital upper limb differences, but their value depends on representative participation. This study examined whether socioeconomic status influences questionnaire response rates within the Australian Hand Difference Register. Using postcode-based Socioeconomic Indexes for Areas, we compared responders and non-responders to registry questionnaires. Families who did not respond were significantly more likely to reside in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas across all four indices examined, although absolute differences were modest. Response rates were highest among families from the most advantaged areas and lowest among those from the most disadvantaged quintiles. Demographic characteristics did not differ between groups. These findings suggest that children from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds are under-represented in the registry, raising concerns regarding equity and generalisability of registry-derived research. papers.title: Reporting of procedural information and data access in surgical robotics across four specialties.
papers.abstract: To distinguish procedural capabilities, observed results, measurement provenance and data-access conditions in surgical robotics publications. We audited 180 retained PubMed publications, 45 per specialty. Eligible original reports evaluated physical surgical robot use. Seventy-two publications underwent separate assessments; 71 remained eligible after adjudication. Five procedural domains were classified by information nature, provenance and access. Descriptive analyses separated physical measurements from observational evidence and examined specialty patterns and sensitivity to evidence definitions. Among 71 publications, 50 (70.4%) described capabilities and 36 (50.7%) reported measured, observed or recalled results. Physical measurements or device-displayed quantities had identified acquisition routes in seven (9.9%), decreasing to five (7.0%) when two boundary evidence types were set aside; five further publications had unclear routes. Direct observations or clinical records contributed results in 26 publications. Four reported temporal curves. Data-availability statements occurred in 38 publications (53.5%); 25 of these offered access on request. Excluding qualitative event-absence evidence reduced reporting to 29/71 (40.8%). Submitted domain-state agreement among all 72 assessed publications was 88.3%; a descriptive check after entry correction yielded 94.2%. Procedural reporting should connect each capability or result to its acquisition source, evidence location and resource-specific access conditions. The distinction between physical measurements, clinical observations and qualitative event absence is central to interpreting robotic performance. A concise core with modality-specific fields could help investigators document these links in protocols, case-report forms and publications. Prospective evaluation should assess consistency, completion burden and whether the record helps readers locate and interpret supporting resources. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261486023.

papers.title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na+ and Ca2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. This review integrates ASIC biophysical properties with their molecular and circuit-level mechanisms in disease, offering a framework to guide future translational efforts targeting ASIC-mediated pathologies.

This single-centre, retrospective, comparative study evaluated pterygomaxillary junction anatomy and separation patterns in 31 patients with repaired CLP who underwent orthognathic surgery, and compared these findings with those of 31 age- and deformity-comparable non-cleft skeletal Class III control patients. The right and left pterygomaxillary regions were assessed separately. Linear and angular measurements were performed on preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images, and separation patterns were classified on 1-month postoperative CBCT images. The groups were similar in age and sex distribution, and all patients had a skeletal Class III deformity. On both sides, pterygomaxillary junction thickness and width were significantly greater in patients with repaired CLP, while medial pterygoid plate length was significantly shorter (all P < 0.05). The right side pterygomaxillary angle was also greater in the CLP patients. Separation patterns were similar on the right side, whereas a significant difference was observed on the left side (P = 0.012), with a higher frequency of type 4 separation in patients with repaired CLP. Additional exploratory subgroup analyses according to cleft morphology showed no significant difference between the lesser and greater segments in unilateral complete cleft patients or between isolated cleft lip and isolated cleft palate subgroups. These findings indicate that repaired CLP is associated with distinct pterygomaxillary junction anatomy and altered separation behaviour, supporting careful preoperative CBCT assessment for surgical planning and risk reduction.

papers.title: Patient-specific customized titanium mesh for alveolar bone regeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesCustomized titanium meshes are increasingly being used for guided bone regeneration (GBR) of complex alveolar ridge deficiencies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their clinical performance with respect to horizontal, vertical and volumetric bone gain, percentage of planned bone volume achieved, healing complications, and implant-related outcomes and, where comparative evidence was available, assessed their performance relative to other GBR approaches.Materials and methodsElectronic databases were searched up to April 15, 2026 to identify randomized and non-randomized comparative studies and prospective or retrospective single-arm studies evaluating customized titanium mesh for alveolar ridge augmentation. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for regenerative, complication, and implant-related outcomes, and comparative evidence was additionally evaluated using network meta-analysis where appropriate. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2), Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. The certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.ResultsThirty reports representing 29 independent studies involving 840 participants and 966 augmented sites were included. The pooled mean vertical and horizontal bone gains were 4.61 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.08 to 5.14) and 5.45 mm (95% CI, 3.97 to 6.94), respectively, while the pooled volumetric bone gain was 1.07 cm³ (95% CI, 0.73 to 1.41). The pooled percentage of planned bone volume achieved was 82.5% (95% CI, 73.1% to 92.0%). Mesh exposure was the most frequent complication, with a pooled rate of 19.75% (95% CI, 14.41% to 26.46%), whereas postoperative infection (2.87%; 95% CI, 1.38% to 5.86%) and implant failure (1.33%; 95% CI, 0.67% to 2.64%) were less common. Network meta-analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences in vertical bone gain between customized titanium mesh and the alternative GBR approaches evaluated. The certainty of the evidence ranged from low to very low.ConclusionsWithin the limitations of the available evidence, customized titanium meshes were associated with clinically relevant alveolar ridge augmentation, while mesh exposure remained relatively frequent. Postoperative infection and implant failure were less frequent. Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate clear superiority over alternative GBR approaches, and the certainty of the available evidence remains low to very low.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

papers.title: Segmented Primary Molar Autotransplantation Following Anterior Tooth Loss In A 10-Year-Old Child: A Novel Surgical Technique.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo report the first clinical application of segmented primary molar autotransplantation as a phase-I biological interim measure within the two-phase transplantation (TPTX) concept, and to describe its short-term clinical and radiographic course in a child who has lost permanent anterior teeth and no longer has primary canines available as donor teeth.Materials and methodsA 10-year-old boy with traumatic loss of the maxillary incisors underwent transplantation of a segmented mandibular primary molar to region 21 after repeated loss of a previously transplanted primary canine. The primary molar was segmented intraorally to obtain a single-root transplantable unit, pulpotomized, adhesively built up, transplanted into the recipient site and stabilized with a semi-rigid titanium splint. The transplant was followed clinically and radiographically over 12 months.ResultsAt 12-month follow-up, the graft showed stable clinical integration with healthy peri-transplant soft tissues and no signs of inflammation. Percussion indicated ankylotic stabilization, and radiographs demonstrated progressive resorptive changes consistent with primary tooth tissue behavior, without periradicular inflammatory resorption.ConclusionsIn this proof-of-concept case, segmented primary molar autotransplantation was feasible and showed a stable course over 12 months. papers.title: Temporomandibular Joint Pseudogout Diagnosed by Arthrocentesis Associated with Peri-Odontoid Calcification: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition disease, also known as pseudogout, rarely involves the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and is often difficult to diagnose because of its nonspecific clinical and radiographic features. In many reported cases, a definitive diagnosis has been established only after biopsy or surgical intervention. An 84-year-old woman presented with swelling and pain in the right preauricular region accompanied by neck pain. Imaging revealed calcified lesions around the right TMJ with joint-space enlargement, as well as peri-odontoid calcification. The differential diagnoses of the TMJ lesion included synovial chondromatosis and pseudogout. Arthrocentesis of the TMJ was performed, and microscopic examination of the aspirated fluid under compensated polarized light microscopy revealed positively birefringent rhomboid crystals, leading to a definitive diagnosis of TMJ pseudogout without the need for surgical biopsy or other invasive intervention. Treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs resulted in rapid symptom resolution, and no recurrence was observed during a 2-year follow-up period. This case highlights that TMJ arthrocentesis can serve as a useful and minimally invasive diagnostic procedure for establishing a definitive diagnosis of pseudogout while potentially avoiding unnecessary surgical biopsy or invasive intervention. In addition, the presence of peri-odontoid calcification may suggest CPPD deposition at multiple anatomical sites.

papers.title: Concomitant Temporomandibular Joint and Orthognathic Surgery in Patients With Dentofacial Deformities: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: The management of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) in patients with dentofacial deformities remains controversial, particularly regarding the role of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) surgery in addition to orthognathic treatment. While orthognathic surgery alone may improve TMD symptoms, some patients may require additional TMJ procedures because of established intra-articular pathology. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate outcomes of TMJ surgery performed in association with orthognathic surgery. Studies including patients with skeletal Class II or III deformities and documented intra-articular TMJ pathology undergoing concomitant surgical management were included. Clinical outcomes including pain, joint sounds, function, maximal interincisal opening (MIO), and quality of life were analyzed. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Four studies comprising 5 cohorts and 155 patients were included. All studies were retrospective and showed low to moderate methodological quality (NOS scores: 8-11/16). Concomitant TMJ and orthognathic surgery was associated with improvement in pain and functional outcomes. MIO increased across all evaluable cohorts, although quantitative synthesis remained limited because of methodological heterogeneity. The largest improvement was observed in patients with severe joint pathology, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis. However, outcome reporting was heterogeneous, and quantitative synthesis was limited. Concomitant TMJ and orthognathic surgery may be associated with symptomatic and functional improvement in carefully selected patients with documented intra-articular TMJ pathology. However, current evidence remains insufficient to determine superiority over orthognathic surgery alone or to compare the effectiveness of different TMJ procedures.

papers.title: Processed Peripheral Nerve Allografts for Reconstruction of Trigeminal Sensory Nerve Injuries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundProcessed peripheral nerve allografts (PNAs) are increasingly used for trigeminal nerve reconstruction, but formally appraised pooled estimates are limited.PurposeTo estimate the pooled proportion of repairs achieving functional sensory recovery (FSR) after PNA reconstruction of trigeminal nerves, overall and by nerve branch, gap length, and repair timing.Data sourcesPubMed/MEDLINE (January 2007 to May 2026), Embase and Scopus (to July 2026), reference lists, ClinicalTrials.gov, and meeting proceedings.Study selectionClinical studies reporting FSR in at least 5 PNA-reconstructed trigeminal nerves were included; case reports, reviews, and animal or cadaver studies were excluded. Two reviewers selected studies independently, resolving disagreements by consensus. Of 142 records (65 unique), 8 (5.6%) were included.Data extraction and synthesisFreeman-Tukey-transformed proportions were pooled with DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; I2 and prediction intervals quantified heterogeneity. Risk of bias was appraised with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tool or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and certainty of evidence was graded. Leave-one-out and industry-independent sensitivity analyses were performed.Main outcomes and measuresFSR (Medical Research Council Scale ≥ S3) per repair at last follow-up (6 to 17.7 months); secondary outcomes were subgroup FSR and adverse events.ResultsEight observational studies (160 subjects; 164 repairs) were included; FSR occurred in 140 (86.4%) of 162 evaluable outcomes. Pooled FSR was 89.5% (95% CI, 82.3 to 95.3%; I2 = 26.1%; P = .2; prediction interval, 72.3 to 99.6%). FSR was 92.2% (95% CI, 80.3 to 99.5%; k = 5 studies; n = 104 repairs) in inferior alveolar nerve (IAN)-only studies and 86.7% (95% CI, 76.1 to 94.9%; k = 3 studies; n = 58 outcomes) in mixed IAN and lingual nerve studies (P = .5). Leave-one-out estimates ranged from 86.2 to 92.0%; the industry-independent estimate was 93.3% (95% CI, 81.4 to 99.9%). No graft-related adverse events were reported; certainty of evidence was low.Conclusions and relevancePNA reconstruction of IAN and lingual nerve gaps of 5 to 70 mm was followed by FSR in 89.5% of repairs (low-certainty evidence). Prospective comparative studies with standardized adverse-event and patient-reported outcomes are warranted.

A P value ResultsOf 17,005 patients screened, 13,333 subjects were analyzed: 6,172 (46.3%) received short-term prophylaxis, and 7,161 (53.7%) received prolonged prophylaxis. The mean (SD) age was 6.5 (9.0) years, and 7,199 (54.0%) were male. Severe SSI occurred in one subject in the prolonged group (overall frequency, 0.008%). papers.title: Natural product integrated metal-organic frameworks for chronic wound healing: From pathological signal responsiveness to on-demand drug delivery.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) possess remarkable structural diversity and broad biological activities, giving them substantial potential in chronic wound therapy. However, unfavorable physicochemical properties and poorly controlled local exposure often limit their therapeutic performance. Integrating NPs with metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offers benefits beyond improved drug delivery. NPs can be encapsulated as cargo, incorporated as coordinating ligands, or immobilized on MOF surfaces, while natural macromolecules may themselves form bioactive dressing matrices. Thus, the key issue is not only which NP is incorporated, but also how its material role affects bioavailability and stage-specific therapeutic function. Centered on NPs, this review establishes a framework for understanding MOF-based wound therapies and explains how NP chemistry and material roles govern responsiveness to endogenous pathological signals or external physical stimuli. These effects are further linked to the changing needs of chronic wound healing, from early control of microbial burden and persistent inflammation to tissue regeneration and extracellular matrix remodeling. By moving beyond the conventional view of NPs as passive cargo, this review provides a unified design rationale for stage-adaptive NP-MOF biomaterials and bioactive dressings.

papers.title: Nano-enabled delivery of Himalayan plant bio-actives for controlling implant-associated inflammation and fibrosis.
papers.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of nano-enabled Himalayan phytotherapeutics targeting implant-associated inflammation and fibrotic capsule formation. Mechanistic synthesis reveals that key bioactives-including Withaferin A, Picrosides I and II, Mangiferin, and Emodin-modulate chronic inflammatory and fibrotic cascades by inhibiting TLR4/NFkB and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, restoring NFE2L2-mediated antioxidant defenses, suppressing TGF-β 1/Smad2/3 signaling, and downregulating α-smooth muscle actin α-SMA) stress fiber formation, collagen type I/III deposition, and matrix metalloproteinase-driven extracellular matrix remodeling. Nanocarrier platforms, including polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, and bioactive hydrogel coatings, significantly enhance phytochemical bioavailability, localized surface retention, and sustained release at biomaterial interfaces. Evidence-tiered evaluation demonstrates robust preclinical efficacy for well-characterized bioactives in rodent foreign body reaction and wound models, whereas evidence for secondary metabolites remains largely extrapolated from general non-implant disease paradigms or preliminary in silico predictions. Computational approaches, including network pharmacology, molecular docking, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence, effectively prioritize bioactive leads and optimize formulation dynamics, but require downstream empirical validation. Critical translational bottlenecks include botanical batch-to-batch composition variability, extract standardization, nanomanufacturing scale-up under Current Good Manufacturing Practice guidelines, long-term degradation and toxicological safety at the implant interface, and complex combination product regulatory approval pathways. Direct evidence for the efficacy and long-term safety of Himalayan plant-derived nanoformulations in implant-associated inflammation and fibrosis remains limited, highlighting the need for standardized formulations, mechanistically rigorous preclinical studies, appropriate implant models, long-term safety assessment, and well-designed clinical investigations.

papers.title: Painful Scars as Pain Generators: A Narrative Review and Case Series of Intralesional Lidocaine Treatment.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Active scars can be defined as "pain generators": the pain associated with them may have an important impact on the patient's quality of life. During the healing process, several local and systemic neurochemical changes occur, leading to alterations at both the tissue and systemic levels, with changes in the central nervous system (CNS) implicated in the development of chronic pain. Clinically, the features that define a scar as a pathological one include increased firmness, increased tissue thickness, and increased reactivity of the skin after palpation. The therapeutic approach, therefore, includes both local treatments that interfere with structural changes in the scar tissue and systemic treatments. Materials and Methods: A critical review of the literature regarding the role of local anesthetics in the clinical management of painful scars has been conducted. The paper also reports a series of cases involving patients affected by painful scars who were successfully treated with local lidocaine injections. A series of five cases of adult patients with active painful scars of post-traumatic and post-surgical etiology were treated with intra-lesional infiltration of 0.5% lidocaine. When appropriate, we associated other techniques. Pain intensity has been assessed using the NRS scale before the start of treatment, at the end of treatment, and at the 3-month follow-up. Results and Discussion: Lidocaine infiltration has been associated with a reduction in pain in patients affected by painful scars, as it might reduce the expression of inflammatory mediators. It could also have a neuromodulatory effect by reducing pain signal transduction. Eventually, a key role is the inhibition of NGF binding to its TrkA receptor. In all patients, we observed a long-lasting reduction in pain symptoms, suggesting that changes had occurred in the tissue and in the peripheral nervous system, and a modulation of central nervous system connectivity had been detected. No complications occurred. Conclusions: Local treatment with intralesional infiltration with 0.5% lidocaine was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in pain intensity in patients with painful post-traumatic and post-surgical scars, maintaining the benefit on pain over time, with no complications.

papers.title: Cellular senescence in skin inflammation: molecular mechanisms and potential clinical implications.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence is increasingly regarded as a mechanism linking chronic tissue stress to persistent skin inflammation. Senescent cells are defined by stable cell-cycle arrest with remodeling of morphology, metabolism, and secretory phenotype, of which the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) is central. Because no single marker is sufficient, senescence in skin requires multiparameter, cell-type-resolved criteria. This Review addresses stress sensing, SASP induction, paracrine propagation, immune evasion, cellular heterogeneity, and therapeutic targeting, stratifying evidence by disease: chronic and diabetic wounds are best supported, whereas in psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, cutaneous lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, and vitiligo the evidence remains largely associative, as SASP-like mediators overlap with cytokine programs from activated keratinocytes, stromal cells, and immune cells. Senescence-targeted interventions are classified as senolytics, senomorphics, or senopreventive/geroprotective strategies, and assessed at marker, SASP, senescent-cell-burden, and disease-outcome levels. It further notes that clinical translation depends on defining senescence-maintained lesion subtypes, establishing combinatorial biomarkers and spatial maps, and validating the efficacy and safety window of local therapies in suitable models and human tissues.

papers.title: Dietary Intake Associated with Periodontitis in Adults: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Background: Periodontitis continues to be a global public health burden that is associated with an increased risk of metabolic diseases such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, and cardiovascular diseases. Basal cell carcinoma shows hierarchically organized arborizing stromal vessels. Bowen disease shows glomerular, horizontally oriented units, whereas actinic keratosis shows milder, grade-dependent remodeling; multimodal imaging remains limited in separating hypertrophic actinic keratosis from early squamous cell carcinoma. Psoriasis shows elongated, regularly distributed dilated papillary loops, distinct from the less organized pattern of eczematous dermatitis. Kaposi sarcoma imaging evidence remains preliminary and does not establish stage-specific vascular criteria. This critical narrative review evaluates whether natural-product pharmacology and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated miRNA biology can be linked credibly in this setting. A structured PubMed search updated through 29 September 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar citation tracking, identified direct human perianal studies, anatomically relevant and infection-relevant animal studies, and mechanistically relevant in vitro and in silico evidence. Core studies were appraised on two separate axes: clinical/model proximity and methodological credibility, including material identity and taxonomic validity, chemical characterization, exposure, comparators and controls, model fidelity, EV characterization, causal miRNA evidence, and assay-interference risk. Direct human ethnopharmacological evidence now includes several randomized postoperative studies, although blinding, material standardization, comparator quality, endpoint selection, and mechanistic depth remain heterogeneous. Early-phase mesenchymal stromal cell EV studies provide perianal feasibility and fistula-closure signals without controlled comparative efficacy. A 2025 Wugu Qilin study provides direct human treatment-associated evidence from wound-fluid vesicle-enriched miRNA profiling involving miR-93-3p/EIF4EBP1, but it did not demonstrate EV-mediated transfer to recipient cells. Astragaloside IV-conditioned endothelial progenitor-cell EV studies provide stronger nonperianal cargo-level evidence, whereas curcumin-loaded macrophage EVs primarily support vesicle-assisted delivery. No study establishes the full causal sequence from chemically defined natural-product exposure through rigorously characterized EV cargo alteration and transfer of a defined miRNA to a necessary recipient-cell effect and improved healing in an anatomically faithful perianal model. Direct clinical and translational evidence is therefore present, but the natural product-EV-miRNA mechanism remains unproven; the most immediate needs are material standardization, clinically derived wound-fluid EV profiling, mixed-biofilm models, causal cargo perturbation, assay-interference controls, and stage-adapted local delivery.

papers.title: Selective Immune Clearance and Lung Repair in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Selective immune clearance could limit pulmonary fibrosis by removing disease-sustaining cells, but its value depends on preserving the capacity of the remaining tissue to repair. This narrative review examines PubMed literature searched through 10 October 2026, prioritizing studies published from 10 October 2024 to 10 October 2026 while retaining relevant earlier investigations. We compare human tissue profiling, immunopeptidomics, cell assays and animal interventions according to target recognition, effector-dependent elimination, treatment phase and retained repair capacity. Vaccination, checkpoint blockade and engineered immune cells provide different combinations of cytotoxicity, altered cell abundance and antifibrotic activity. However, repair-associated senescence and conflicting FAP-targeting outcomes show why marker expression alone cannot determine which cells should be removed. Epithelial proliferation and inferred cell trajectories are therefore assessed separately from lineage-supported differentiation, alveolar organization and sustained barrier, vascular and physiological recovery. The available studies do not yet establish that selective clearance produces lasting alveolar recovery, and clinical benefit in IPF remains unproven. Functional target validation, treatment after fibrosis is established, and follow-up after treatment withdrawal are priorities for translation.

papers.title: From Fixed Lineage to Dynamic States: Fibro-Adipogenic Progenitors in Skeletal Muscle Regeneration, Fibrosis, and Fibrofatty Degeneration.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle repair depends on coordinated interactions among muscle stem cells, immune cells, extracellular matrix, and resident stromal cells. A key stromal population, fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), has attracted considerable attention. Yet FAPs are not a fixed mesenchymal lineage. They form a plastic, heterogeneous compartment with context-dependent functional states that shift with injury stage, anatomical site, disease, and species. Understanding what drives this plasticity is essential. This review examines how biochemical, inflammatory, mechanical, and epigenetic signals shape FAP states. We synthesize evidence from multiple species, including mouse, human, bovine, porcine, and camel muscle systems. Four regulatory modules are considered: TGF-β/PDGFRα signaling and immune crosstalk, canonical and non-canonical Wnt pathways, epigenetic regulation, and extracellular matrix mechanotransduction. Through these pathways, FAPs adopt distinct functional programs. These include homeostatic maintenance, reparative support, fibrogenic activation, adipogenic differentiation, inflammatory response, and senescence. Each program differentially influences muscle stem cell function and tissue remodeling outcomes. These programs reflect context-dependent FAP states, not a uniform lineage with fixed functions. Several concepts require clarification. We emphasize that fibrogenic and adipogenic programs can be differentially regulated yet coexist within diseased muscle, and that pathological FAP states may retain context-dependent reversibility. These insights clarify the constraints on cross-species translation and inform the design of stage-matched, context-appropriate, or combinatorial FAP-directed therapeutic strategies for muscle disease.

papers.title: Vitreous Transcriptomics in Diabetic Retinopathy: Current Research and Future Prospects.
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet the molecular mechanisms behind its vision-threatening complications remain not fully understood. Transcriptomics enables the study of these processes through active gene expression, providing a pathway to the discovery of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Vitreous humour is commonly affected in numerous retinal pathologies, including DR, and is accessible through pars plana vitrectomy, making it a good candidate for transcriptomics research. Following PubMed and Embase search, 18 articles on vitreous transcriptomics were included. They were subclassified into themes of non-coding RNA, RNA methylation, angiogenesis, inflammation and fibrosis. We concluded that vitreous transcriptomics has the potential to influence future DR diagnostics and therapeutics. However, current evidence is limited by underpowered studies and lack of standardised protocols.

papers.title: Nanomedicine-Enhanced CAR-Engineered Immunotherapy for Lung Cancer: Focusing on Multimodal Strategies and Precision Therapy.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a major therapeutic challenge because of its molecular and antigenic heterogeneity, rapid evolution, treatment resistance, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed the treatment of hematological malignancies, its efficacy in lung cancer remains constrained by antigen heterogeneity, poor tumor trafficking and infiltration, T-cell dysfunction, suppressive stromal and myeloid compartments, manufacturing complexity, and pulmonary on-target off-tumor toxicity. Nanomedicine offers a versatile platform to address these barriers by improving CAR-T manufacturing and functional fitness, enabling targeted delivery of nucleic acids and immunomodulators, remodeling the TME, enhancing local accumulation and controlled activation, and supporting transient in situ generation of CAR-engineered immune cells. This review integrates these advances within a Route-Antigen-Microenvironment-Programming (RAMP) framework and emphasizes the mechanistic interdependence among delivery route, target selection, local tumor ecology, and CAR generation and control. We examine the antigen landscapes of non-small-cell and small-cell lung cancer and propose a quantitative framework for antigen selection that incorporates antigen density, spatial and temporal heterogeneity, normal-tissue safety, and engineering compensability. We further discuss nanotechnology-assisted manufacturing, cell-surface nanobackpacks, tumor preconditioning, local biomaterial reservoirs, in vivo CAR programming, pulmonary delivery, multimodal therapy, and theranostic monitoring. Most nano-enabled approaches are still supported primarily by preclinical studies or evidence from non-lung-cancer settings, underscoring the need for standardized assessment of biodistribution, reproducibility, immunogenicity, pulmonary safety, and long-term material fate. Integrating quantitative antigen profiling with biodegradable and controllable materials and lung-relevant translational models may help advance CAR-engineered immunotherapy toward a spatially controlled, dynamically monitored, and personalized therapeutic platform for lung cancer.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Zygomatic implants are commonly used to rehabilitate atrophic maxillae and maxillary defects, offering quicker prosthesis placement than bone grafting, but their placement requires technical precision due to the complexity of the zygomatic region. papers.title: Advances and Future Perspectives on Chitosan-Based Hydrogels for Bone Regeneration in Periodontitis-Associated Defects.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis-triggered alveolar bone loss is an irreversible pathological lesion that remains challenging to regenerate in clinical practice. Functionally modified chitosan (CS) hydrogels combine favorable biocompatibility, tunable biodegradability, intrinsic antibacterial activity, and immunomodulatory properties, rendering them promising scaffolds for the repair of inflammatory bone defects. This review summarizes advances over the past five years in the development of functionalized CS hydrogels for periodontitis-associated alveolar bone regeneration. We categorize and compare four mainstream modification strategies for CS: biomimetic structural design, inflammatory immunoregulation, stimuli-responsive controlled release, and mechanical microenvironment adaptation. Beyond hydrogels, chemically modified CS in diverse forms (membranes, bulk scaffolds, micro/nanoparticles, and surface coatings) is also discussed. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate on the core regenerative mechanisms of modified CS hydrogels, including antibacterial defense, immune microenvironment remodeling, osteogenic activation, and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Unlike most previous reviews covering CS biomaterials, the present work specifically focuses on the challenges of bone regeneration under periodontitis-related inflammatory conditions, with a small set of other bone regeneration studies included as supporting references. It examines the key limitations of current investigations-particularly those concerning mechanical matching, sustained anti-inflammatory efficacy, and clinical translatability-and outlines targeted research directions involving structural optimization, multistage cascade regulation, and personalized clinical translation. Overall, this review provides a theoretical framework and practical design strategies for developing high-performance CS-based hydrogels toward periodontal bone defect regeneration.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The complex nature of endodontic/periodontal lesions complicates treatment prognosis, making long-term tooth survival challenging to predict. papers.title: Classification of brain tumors using pseudobulk spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Abstract Transcriptomic classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors is emerging as a diagnostic adjunct. However, conventional bulk sequencing requires multiple tissue sections, which is challenging when biopsy material is limited or diffuse infiltration dilutes the neoplastic signal. In cases with low kNN confidence, tumor-cluster enrichment improved concordance from 60% to 76%. Pseudobulk aggregation of spatial transcriptomics data from a single tissue section can therefore yield diagnostically informative classifications using existing classifiers, with potential for tissue-limited specimens and infiltrative tumors.

papers.title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units—cells, bins or multicellular spots—into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p -values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene–gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p -values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

papers.title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome
papers.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86+ switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.

papers.title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)
papers.abstract: BackgroundSynovial inflammation in psoriatic arthritis (PsA) lacks a validated histological classification framework. Current approaches apply rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovial pathotypes to PsA, which overlooks immunobiological differences between the diseases and limits the predictive power of tissue stratification. MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were obtained from 61 patients with PsA (n=22), seropositive RA (n=23), seronegative RA (n=10), and other inflammatory arthritides (n=6). Sections underwent multi-modal staining, including H&E, picrosirius red, and immunohisto-chemistry for CD3, CD20, CD68, CD138, and CD31. Whole-slide digital image analysis and automated pixel classifiers quantified cellular and stromal metrics. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified intrinsic PsA pathotypes, which were correlated with clinical disease activity, radiographic osteoarthritis (OA), and longitudinal treatment responses. FindingsWhile a subset of PsA patients shared an inflammatory signature with seropositive RA, unsupervised clustering of the PsA cohort revealed three distinct, novel pathotypes: Dense Myeloid (macrophage-driven), Fibro-Stromal (fibrosis and pauci-immune), and Angio-Lymphoid (hypervascular with significant CD138+ plasma cell infiltration). Pathotypes were independent of treatment and concurrent radiographic knee OA. The Fibro-Stromal pathotype correlated with significantly higher cutaneous psoriasis severity. Longitudinally, patients with the Fibro-Stromal pathotype exhibited a trend toward lower treatment response (44%) following standard interventions (methotrexate or TNF inhibitors) compared to the Dense Myeloid (50%) and Angio-Lymphoid (80%) pathotypes. InterpretationWe present the first computationally derived synovial pathotypes specific to PsA, revealing distinct plasma cell and fibrotic architectures not captured by RA-centric models. To enable clinical translation, we distilled these findings into a pragmatic, four-marker diagnostic decision tree (CD31, CD68, CD138, and picrosirius red) designed for routine histopathology workflows, providing a staging ground for biomarker-stratified clinical trials in PsA. FundingFunding from the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre: Manchester, Arthritis UK, the Wellcome Trust, Brit-PACT, the National Psoriasis Foundation, and the Medical Research Council. papers.title: Single-cell profiling of human plaques reveals cellular and molecular signatures of symptomatic atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability drives ischemic cardiovascular events, yet the cellular and molecular signatures distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic human plaques remain poorly defined. papers.title: DisCell: Separating Spillover from Niche Response in Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution measures every cell in its place in the tissue, but diffusion and segmentation errors also add transcripts of neighboring cells to a cell’s counts. This spillover makes a cell resemble its neighbors, and a response to the niche makes cells in the same niche resemble each other. Both tie a cell’s expression to its surroundings. The count data alone cannot tell the two apart. Findings: from single-cell transcriptomes, such as a gene program that is higher in one niche than in another or signaling genes that change depending on the neighborhood, may therefore be artifacts of spillover. Current models describe a cell by its intrinsic state together with either its niche response or spillover, but none models all three. We present DisCell, the first method that models all three components jointly and measures how robust each finding is to spillover. DisCell is a generative model that describes single-cell gene expression profiles in terms of two latent variables, an intrinsic state and a response to the niche, and adds spillover from its neighbors as a separate term. DisCell fits the model at increasing levels of spillover and recomputes each finding on the spillover-free expression to see how much spillover it withstands. DisCell also estimates the most spillover a section can contain, and a finding that holds even at that amount is not explained by spillover. In simulated tissue, DisCell recovers each cell’s intrinsic state and response and tells findings created by spillover apart from genuine responses. On five sections of ovarian and lung tissue, the intrinsic state keeps more of each cell’s own properties, measured by its cell-cycle phase, than any competing method that holds as little of its neighborhood. Within each cell type, the model partitions the variation of each gene into intrinsic state, niche response and spillover. Using DisCell, we rank findings about niches by their robustness to spillover and confirm that a previously reported finding withstands spillover, that esophageal cancer cells in niches infiltrated by immune or stromal cells express more of an epithelial–mesenchymal transition program. DisCell also predicts what the gene expression of a cell type would be in another niche, with its spillover part separated, at lower error on most tasks than the competing method built for this purpose. Training the model takes under ten minutes on one consumer GPU for sections of up to 400,000 cells.

papers.title: Reinvigorating immunotherapy: harnessing tumor microenvironment modulation for enhanced cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of multiple malignancies, yet primary and acquired resistance remain major barriers to attaining durable clinical benefit. We also review clinical strategies for remodeling the TME to increase the efficacy of immunotherapeutic approaches. Additionally, we discuss the opportunities and challenges associated with TME remodeling, including safety considerations, emerging biomarkers, and rational combination strategies. We propose that future TME-targeted therapies should transition from component-oriented interventions to dynamic and mechanism-matched strategies guided by dominant resistance axes. papers.title: PLA2G2A across tumor compartments and its relevance to drug resistance.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance in cancer is shaped not only by tumor-cell-intrinsic mutations but also by spatially organized microenvironmental states. PLA2G2A, encoding group IIA secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2-IIA), is usually discussed as an inflammatory lipid enzyme; however, its cancer relevance depends strongly on cellular source, localization and disease stage. Several cancer studies provide PLA2G2A-specific functional evidence for invasion, proliferation/stemness, non-catalytic signaling or T-cell dysfunction, but direct demonstration that PLA2G2A changes response to a defined anticancer therapy remains sparse. The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cancer-associated fibroblast study provides the strongest resistance-proximal immune-functional evidence, whereas mucinous colorectal extracellular vesicles, ovarian ascites, invasive-front fibroblasts, treatment-remodeled stroma and prognostic signatures require more direct therapy-response validation. Gastric and intestinal epithelial data further caution that PLA2G2A may accompany differentiation, invasion restraint, antimicrobial defense or barrier protection. We therefore argue against treating PLA2G2A as a universal oncogenic target. Instead, it should be advanced as a mechanism-matched biomarker or therapeutic hypothesis only when compartment, biochemical-output, functional and perturbational evidence converge.

papers.abstract: BackgroundThe oral cavity is continuously exposed to environmental, lifestyle-related, microbial, and systemic influences capable of altering tissue homeostasis and contributing to chronic oral disease. The most mature human evidence concerned conventional tobacco smoking and selected carcinogenic exposures, whereas associations involving air pollution, heavy metals, occupational toxicants, electronic cigarettes, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and emerging contaminants showed greater heterogeneity and, for several outcomes, relied substantially on observational, experimental, or mechanistic evidence. papers.abstract: Filtering bleb scarring after glaucoma filtration surgery (GFS) remains the leading cause of surgical failure, and current antimetabolites are limited by non-selective cytotoxicity that restricts their long-term use. papers.title: Public omics data reuse in gastric cancer: from discovery abundance to translational evidence.
papers.abstract: Public-omics data are now widely reused in gastric cancer bioinformatics. Resources such as The Cancer Genome Atlas stomach adenocarcinoma cohort (TCGA-STAD), the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), cBioPortal, proteogenomic cohorts, single-cell atlases, and spatial datasets make secondary analysis fast and inexpensive. They are used to study tumor biology, biomarkers, prognosis, therapy-response hypotheses, and tumor-microenvironment states. A major limitation in this literature is not data access. It is evidentiary dilution. Many studies reuse similar cohorts and analytical pipelines. They then produce additional gene lists or risk signatures without a corresponding improvement in independent validation, interpretation, or clinical relevance. This methodological narrative review synthesizes public-omics secondary analysis in gastric cancer from methodological, translational, and reproducibility-oriented perspectives, supported by reproducible PubMed database scans and public metadata checks conducted through 2026-06-30; both are descriptive signals and are not formal quality appraisals. The review has three aims. The first aim is to classify reusable public data resources and the recurring analytical workflows built on them. The second aim is to use prognostic modeling as a stress test for leakage, overfitting, weak validation, and overinterpreted clinical value. The third aim is to propose GC-PROVE, a five-domain appraisal framework covering problem anchoring, resource provenance, omics workflow transparency, validation hierarchy, and evidence restraint. Public-omics research is most useful when it produces auditable evidence, external validation, biological triangulation, and a clear clinical context.

papers.title: Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart.
papers.abstract: The immune-fibrotic axis functions as a vicious feedback loop where age-related chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation (inflammaging) drives maladaptive tissue repair and fibrosis, while senescent fibrotic cells in turn amplify systemic inflammation. The major biological significance of these findings is that cardiac immune-fibrotic remodeling is not a uniform, heart-wide process. Instead, it varies with cell type, with valves and aorta emerging as major sites where age-associated programs converge to progressively compromise cardiac structure and function.

papers.title: Identifying multi-omics spatial domains via masked autoencoder and diffusion-based latent regularization with SpaMEDM.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omics data provide complementary molecular views of tissue organization. papers.title: OncoSpot enables benchmarking of cancer spatial transcriptomics methods across tumor evolutionary modes

papers.title: Unified cell segmentation for spatial transcriptomics via transcript reassignment

papers.title: Development of a multi-organ single-cell atlas of systemic sclerosis reveals shared and tissue-specific pathogenic pathways

In addition, perivascular and mitotic fibroblast subpopulations exhibited both profibrotic and inflammatory signatures, including interferon- and IL-2-related signalling programmes. papers.title: Kontext: Kernel-based method bridging spatial domain identification and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of biological tissues is characterized by spatial domains: regions with coherent transcriptional and anatomical properties, heavily influenced by local cell-cell interactions. Although identifying spatial domains is a common task in spatial transcriptomics, most existing methods provide limited mechanistic insight into their organization. We present Kontext, a kernel-based framework that jointly represents cells and their local environments, enabling the identification of spatial domains grounded in their underlying ligand-receptor interactions. This representation further provides complementary outputs for characterizing cellular microenvironments, spatial niches, and sender-receiver communication patterns. Kontext outperforms state-of-the-art methods in recovering reference domain annotations across several spatial transcriptomics technologies and biological models, while offering improved computational efficiency and scalability. Applying Kontext on a Xenium temporal mouse heart cryoinjury dataset, we characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of the injury and identify an undescribed sustained activity of the complement system in the communication between fibroblasts and macrophages during scar maturation. In a million-cell three-dimensional Open-ST dataset of human metastatic lymph node tissue, we combine spatial domain identification and niche analysis to define the boundary region between the tumor and its microenvironment, revealing distinct communication patterns between this interface and the tumor core.

papers.title: The gut-bone axis: gut microbiota dysbiosis and dental implant failures – Is there a link? - A narrative review
papers.abstract: Introduction: The gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in systemic health, particularly in bone metabolism and periodontal integrity, through the gut–bone axis. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may indirectly contribute to dental implant failure by disrupting bone homeostasis and aggravating periodontal disease. Despite growing recognition of this relationship, comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms and therapeutic strategies remains limited. This review explores the available biological evidence on the impact of gut microbiota dysbiosis on dental implant failures. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and related databases was performed following PRISMA guidelines. Studies addressing the gut microbiota–bone health connection, gut microbiota–periodontium interactions, and their collective influence on implant success were included. Screening was based on predefined criteria, with data extraction focusing on mechanisms through which dysbiosis affects osseointegration and peri-implant health. Results The review revealed a strong association between gut dysbiosis and altered bone metabolism, impairing osseointegration and raising the risk of implant failure. Gut dysbiosis also exacerbated periodontal inflammation, predisposing to peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis. Non-invasive strategies such as probiotics, prebiotics, and targeted dietary modifications showed promise in restoring microbial balance, attenuating systemic inflammation, and supporting peri-implant tissue health. However, wide heterogeneity in study design and methodology restricted the strength and comparability of available evidence. Conclusion Gut microbiota dysbiosis is an emerging and underrecognized risk factor for implant failure. Modulating dysbiosis through non-invasive interventions may enhance osseointegration and peri-implant tissue integrity. Nevertheless, most current evidence arises from preclinical or small-scale human studies, highlighting the urgent need for robust, large-scale clinical trials.

papers.title: CATFISHR: integration of transcriptome and inferred CNV profiles for comprehensive malignant cell identification
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Malignant cell identification in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) remains challenging because transcriptomic cell typing, somatic variant detection and inferred copy-number approaches each have modality-specific limitations. In several cohorts, Hidden cells were transcriptionally closer to benchmark malignant than non-malignant compartments; in Visium data, sampled Hidden spots contained histologist-confirmed morphologically malignant cells. CATFISHR reduces missed malignant calls while preserving rare, transitional and benchmark-discordant populations for downstream investigation. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT

papers.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex

papers.title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts-Orchestrated Immune Remodeling as a Key Driver in Liver Cancer.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) develop within a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by chronic inflammation, extensive stromal remodeling, and impaired antitumor immunity. Advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies have revealed substantial CAF heterogeneity and identified distinct CAF subsets with specialized immunomodulatory functions. These findings have uncovered novel therapeutic opportunities, including CAF-targeted approaches, extracellular matrix normalization, and strategies aimed at reprogramming CAF plasticity. Overall, CAFs are central orchestrators of immune remodeling in liver cancer and contribute to the establishment of an immunosuppressive microenvironment that supports tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Targeting CAF-driven stromal-immune interactions may enhance antitumor immunity and improve the efficacy of current and emerging immunotherapies in HCC and iCCA.

papers.title: Platform Switching with Dental Implants: What Have We Learned Over the Past 20 Years?
papers.abstract: Since its formal description in 2006, platform switching has evolved from a single clinical obser-vation into a widely investigated technique and a recognized design feature in implant dentistry. Numerous systematic reviews and meta-analyses, drawing on randomized controlled trials, have ex-amined it. The geometric mechanism-medial repositioning of the inflammatory cell infiltrate at the microgap of the implant-abutment junction-is supported by histologic and immunohistochemical studies, while biomechanical analyses have characterized the associated load-transfer trade-offs. The effect requires establishing the platform-switched configuration at the placement of a heal-ing abutment and maintaining it thereafter. Recent reviews have reported positive soft tissue and esthetic outcomes, and the approach is now widely integrated in contemporary implant systems, combining platform switching with internal connections and subcrestal placement. This commen-tary reviews that progression, from clinical observation to standard implant feature, and reframes platform switching as one geometric expression of a broader biologic principle: Marginal bone sta-bility depends on the organization and inflammatory containment of the supracrestal peri-implant tissues and on the spatial separation (horizontal and vertical) between the inflammatory challenge and bone. It proposes framing the implant-abutment interface as a biologic boundary, identifies unresolved questions after 20 years, and outlines directions for future research.

papers.title: Enhancing cell type deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics through incorporating multiple reference panels.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) captures gene expression with spatial context but often at resolutions where each spatial location contains multiple cells. Deconvolution of cell-type proportions is therefore essential, yet existing methods typically rely on a single scRNA-seq reference, limiting accuracy when references are incomplete or mismatched especially in complex tissues. These limitations highlight the need for a framework that can integrate multiple references while leveraging spatial information. We introduce SWIMR (Spatially Weighted Integration for Multi-Reference deconvolution), a statistical framework that integrates multiple scRNA-seq references while accounting for spatial correlations. SWIMR models each spatial location as a weighted combination of references, with both cell-type proportions and reference weights varying across tissue locations. Across comprehensive simulations and diverse ST datasets, SWIMR consistently outperformed single-reference approaches. In developing human heart tissue, it recovered ground-truth cell-type compositions with the highest accuracy. In mouse embryo and liver cancer, it leveraged context-specific references to resolve organ-specific cell types and increase sensitivity for biologically relevant pathways. Together, these results establish SWIMR as a robust framework for multi-reference deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: NRF2 in hypertrophic scarring: A stage-dependent redox hub poised between resolution and persistence.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scarring (HTS) is a fibroproliferative outcome of deep dermal injury, reflecting failed scar resolution rather than collagen excess alone. Sustained oxidative and inflammatory signaling is a prominent feature of HTS.
