papers.title: Live Spatial Transcriptomics Enables Longitudinal Tissue Mapping
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has become an important technology in biomedical research by preserving the spatial context of gene expression in tissues and enabling the study of cellular states and interactions in situ . However, most existing methods provide only static snapshots of individual tissue specimens, requiring inference of the molecular dynamics underlying development, disease progression, and therapeutic response from different specimens rather than direct tracking in the same living tissue. Here, we introduce Live Spatial Transcriptomics (Live-ST), a technology that enables longitudinal, transcriptome-wide profiling of living tissue. Live-ST combines electroporation-based intracellular sampling and spatial barcoding to enable repeated, spatially resolved mRNA measurements in intact living tissue through next-generation sequencing. We demonstrate its capabilities by (i) benchmarking spatial mRNA capture in patterned two-dimensional cell systems, (ii) spatially profiling transcriptomes in intact, patient-derived living melanoma tissues while preserving tissue viability, and (iii) longitudinally tracking drug-response dynamics within the tumor microenvironment. Together, Live-ST enables repeated, non-destructive measurements of spatial gene expression, providing a new framework for studying dynamic tissue biology in native physiological and pathological contexts.

papers.title: Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean
papers.abstract: Deep learning has enabled virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology, offering a scalable approach to molecular profiling of routinely archived tissue without molecular assays. However, reliable uncertainty estimates are essential for identifying potentially inaccurate predictions, and it remains unclear whether existing methods provide useful information about prediction reliability. We evaluate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using probabilistic likelihoods and approximate Bayesian methods alongside histology-free and training-free baselines, assessing both calibration and error informativeness. Moreover, good calibration does not imply informative uncertainty, with simple distributions fitted without histology achieving comparable calibration. We therefore distinguish calibrated from informative uncertainty and argue that uncertainty should provide information about prediction error beyond the predicted mean. papers.title: A biological approach for corticoperiosteal free flaps in mandibular reconstruction without rigid fixation: the wrapping technique.
papers.abstract: Mandibular reconstruction in irradiated or otherwise compromised bone environments requires both mechanical stability and biological revitalization of devitalized tissue. papers.title: Treatment Impact on Inflammatory Markers in Patients with Asthma and Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.
papers.abstract: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) is a type 2 inflammatory disorder resulting from an exaggerated immune response to Aspergillus species, most frequently A. fumigatus, and occurring most commonly in patients with asthma. Accordingly, current guidelines incorporate total IgE into a multidimensional assessment rather than interpreting it in isolation. Nevertheless, changes in total IgE may be discordant with clinical and radiological improvement and can be difficult to interpret during anti-IgE therapy or biologics targeting interleukin (IL)-4/IL-13 or thymic stromal lymphopoietin pathways. A. fumigatus-specific IgE and IgG show inconsistent treatment-related trajectories. Peripheral blood eosinophil counts and fractional exhaled nitric oxide are strongly dependent on treatment mechanisms and may reflect pharmacodynamic target engagement rather than overall ABPA activity. Emerging biomarkers, including recombinant A. fumigatus allergens, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine, periostin, eotaxin, carcinoembryonic antigen, and eosinophil-derived neurotoxin, provide additional mechanistic insights. However, none have demonstrated sufficient longitudinal validation for routine monitoring. Overall, biomarker trajectories in ABPA are strongly influenced by treatment mechanisms and may be dissociated from clinical benefit. Although several inflammatory markers decline with treatment, no individual marker is sufficiently sensitive and specific to serve as a universal marker of immune response. Treatment response should be assessed by integrating clinical and radiological improvement with appropriately interpreted immunological biomarkers rather than relying on a single laboratory measurement. Future studies should develop and validate treatment-specific biomarker signatures that distinguish pharmacodynamic target engagement from genuine control of ABPA activity.

papers.title: Robotic applications in orthognathic surgery: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Orthognathic surgery has increasingly incorporated digital technologies to improve accuracy and reproducibility, and robotic systems have recently emerged as a potential extension of these advances. This scoping review aimed to comprehensively map and synthesize the existing literature on robotic applications in orthognathic surgery, with emphasis on the types of robotic systems, their functional roles, level of clinical translation, and current limitations. The included studies most consistently reported improvement in geometric accuracy and reproducibility of plan-to-execution transfer, particularly for maxillary positioning and linear osteotomies under surgeon supervision, with performance generally comparable to established digital techniques rather than superior. Clinical adoption remains limited by small patient cohorts, lack of long-term outcome data, and insufficient comparative evidence. Overall, robotic technology represents a promising, task-specific adjunct in orthognathic surgery, but current evidence does not support routine replacement of established digital workflows. Future research should prioritize comparative clinical trials, standardized outcome reporting, and improved integration into surgical workflows to better define the clinical value of robotics in orthognathic surgery.

papers.title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain.
papers.abstract: AbstractSpontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation. Emerging evidence now challenges this view. Converging data from pharmacology, neural recordings, and systems-level causal manipulations indicate that spontaneous and stimulus-evoked pain arise from substantially dissociable molecular, cellular, and circuit substrates. Injured-fiber-derived ectopic activity within specific sensory neuron subtypes serves as a dominant peripheral generator of spontaneous pain, whereas cellularly distinct, intact spared-fiber pathways mediate stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity. At spinal and supraspinal levels, spontaneous pain preferentially engages affective-salience networks during pain chronification and may ultimately become stabilized within higher-order circuitry-while remaining dynamically coupled to afferent input. This mechanistic delineation carries critical translational implications. Current diagnostic and treatment guidelines rarely differentiate symptom domains, and most therapies have been validated primarily using stimulus-evoked or overall pain intensity endpoints-potentially contributing to a mechanism-therapy mismatch and variable efficacy. We argue that spontaneous neuropathic pain should be defined as a separate symptom domain rather than considered as a spontaneous manifestation of evoked pain mechanisms. This recognition demands longitudinal, biomarker-informed phenotyping to capture its persistent and fluctuating nature, and thereby enable robust mechanistic dissection at peripheral, spinal, and cortical nodes. Reframing spontaneous neuropathic pain along these lines will provide a foundation for precision therapeutics that target defined cell types, specific molecular drivers, and maladaptive network states-enabling mechanism-based, symptom-aligned treatments.

papers.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases.
papers.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

papers.title: Sonodynamic Therapy in Periodontitis: From Mechanisms to Biomaterial-Based Innovations.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a common chronic inflammatory disease driven by pathogenic biofilms, leading to progressive periodontal tissue destruction and systemic health risks. Conventional therapies often fail to eradicate biofilms in deep periodontal pockets, promote antimicrobial resistance and offer limited regenerative potential. Advances in biomaterials address these barriers by engineering high-performance sonosensitizers to enhance ROS efficiency, developing delivery systems to improve solubility and prolonged retention and integrating multimodal antibacterial and regenerative functions. This review summarizes the mechanistic basis of SDT with recent advances in sonosensitizer engineering, local delivery platforms, synergistic therapies, and multifunctional biomaterials, thereby linking antimicrobial performance to periodontal tissue regeneration. We further identify hypoxia, delivery efficiency, biosafety and the lack of standardized evaluation as key translational challenges, and propose future directions including AI-guided sonosensitizer design, precision delivery systems, and CRISPR-assisted antimicrobial combination strategies to accelerate the clinical translation of SDT for periodontitis management.

papers.title: Spatial determinants of pathological complete response and residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy is associated with favorable outcomes in breast cancer, yet differences in response cannot be explained by immune-cell abundance alone. Disruption at any stage may preserve resistant tumor regions despite substantial overall immune infiltration. Current evidence indicates that immune-cell positioning, multicellular organization, and the spatial distribution of stromal, vascular, and metabolic constraints can provide information beyond conventional cell-density measurements. However, the strength and clinical meaning of these associations vary according to breast cancer subtype, treatment regimen, sampling time point, and analytical platform. Pretreatment tissue, early on-treatment samples, and surgical residual disease address distinct baseline response-associated, pharmacodynamic, and prognostic questions and should therefore be interpreted separately. Residual disease represents a treatment-selected ecosystem rather than simply a smaller version of the untreated tumor. We integrate available evidence into a time-resolved framework linking baseline spatial architecture, treatment-related remodeling, residual disease organization, and subsequent clinical outcome. Translation into clinical practice will require standardized spatial definitions and measurements, reproducible assessment of organized immune structures, subtype- and regimen-specific validation, and demonstration of added value beyond established pathological indicators. Spatially resolved analysis may improve understanding of heterogeneous neoadjuvant responses and support more precise post-treatment risk assessment.

papers.title: Effects of SGLT2 inhibition on cardiac remodeling and heart failure development in aortic stenosis rats.
papers.abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is increasingly prevalent in ageing populations, yet no pharmacological therapy has been shown to modify its progression to heart failure (HF). AS was associated with reduced activity of energy metabolism enzymes, which was not restored by empagliflozin. Collectively, these findings identify oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodeling, and transcriptional reprogramming as mechanisms underlying cardiac dysfunction in AS. Empagliflozin mitigates cardiac remodeling and HF progression and modulates fibrosis and gene networks regulating cardiac function. These data highlight SGLT2 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in pressure overload-induced heart failure.

papers.title: Hierarchical platform of BMP-2 by ZIF-8 encapsulation and ACP coating within a base-prepared chitosan hydrogel for alveolar bone repair.
papers.abstract: Alveolar bone defect repair presents a formidable clinical challenge due to limited self-repair capacity. papers.title: The sirtuin family: from mechanisms to therapy.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRT1-SIRT7) are evolutionarily conserved NAD+-dependent deacylases that function as metabolic sensors, coupling cellular metabolic state to epigenetic, transcriptional and post-translational regulatory programs across distinct subcellular compartments. Despite two decades of research, isoform- and disease-specific aspects remain poorly integrated, limiting both conceptual clarity and therapeutic translation. This review synthesizes recent advances in sirtuin biology into a family-wide framework. Rather than functioning as isolated longevity factors, sirtuins operate as a distributed compartmentalized regulatory network in which nuclear SIRT1, SIRT6 and SIRT7, cytosolic SIRT2 and mitochondrial SIRT3, SIRT4 and SIRT5 collectively govern glucose and lipid metabolism, mitochondrial quality control, autophagy, inflammation and immune tolerance. This network operates across metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer, where dysregulated sirtuin signalling influences disease development in a disease- and tissue-specific manner. Therapeutic strategies are evaluated, ranging from isoform-selective small-molecule modulators and NAD+-targeted interventions to emerging protein-degradation approaches, with isoform selectivity, off-target effects and the systemic consequences of NAD+ modulation identified as key translational barriers that have contributed to heterogeneous clinical outcomes. Viewing sirtuins as a context-sensitive compartmentalized network, not isolated targets, offers a coherent framework to guide mechanistic interrogation and the design of more precise sirtuin-based therapies, with priority areas including tissue-selective degradation and network-level biomarkers.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.

Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.
